Iteration 1/25, stage explore, attempt 1.
Research goal: investigate which measured predictors and subgroups are associated with scientifically meaningful differences in dependency_BRAF (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_DHX9 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_EGFR (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_ERBB2 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_KIF18A (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_KRAS (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_MDM2 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_NFE2L2 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_POLR2A (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_RIT1 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_RPL11 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_SMARCA2 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_STAT3 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_TMED10 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_USP7 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_WRN (CRISPR dependency score). Use the supplied dataset to discover and follow up comparisons, assess effect sizes and uncertainty, and decide which conclusions the evidence supports. Use independent validation when useful and distinguish findings in this dataset from claims about causality or generalizability.
Each iteration proceeds through explore (propose comparisons), analyze (request tests), appraise (assess the resulting discovery evidence and optionally request validation), and synthesize (assess validation and update conclusions and plans).

Study instructions:
Investigate diverse, scientifically meaningful comparisons and use previous
results to allocate further investigation. Broad exploration and focused follow-up are both useful
throughout the run. Assess discoveries in this supplied dataset and use independent validation when
useful. Biological interpretation and generalizability may remain uncertain.

Register comparisons, anticipated directions, and initial assessments before requesting analyses.
The controller assigns claim references. For a changed claim, propose a new comparison and link
refinements to the earlier parent claim.
Clinical log_pfs_months is natural log progression-free survival in months, fully observed without
censoring. Dependency scores are continuous; more negative values mean stronger dependency.
Research signatures are constructed standardized assays in arbitrary units. Research markers D, E,
and F are constructed binary assays with no assigned gene, pathway, or clinical role.
A mean_difference is exposed minus comparator within eligibility and subgroup. An interaction
subtracts that comparison in the subgroup complement in the same eligible population.
Use your scientific judgment to assess the size, uncertainty, and importance of each effect
and decide which conclusions the evidence supports. Explain your reasoning in the narrative.
Returned estimates and intervals are ALREADY SIGNED to the indicated hypothesis direction. Do not
multiply them by direction again. For example, raw -0.4 with direction -1 is reported as +0.4.
Discovery analyses use 95% Welch intervals and need at least 20 observations in every
comparison cell.

Each iteration has explore, analyze, appraise, and synthesize stages. Every stage may register
hypotheses for later analysis. Analyze selects up to 12 previously registered hypotheses.
Appraise assesses every new discovery result, records active/deferred/closed investigation, and may
request validation after considering those results. At most one new voluntary validation request
is allowed per iteration and ten per run. Cached requests reuse the same evidence. The evaluator
may also deliver scheduled validation during the run. Independent intervals account for the maximum
number of validation comparisons in the run. Results arrive before synthesis. Assess newly released
validation immediately in synthesis and explicitly reassess the original claim when its response
deadline appears in the context, even if you also investigate a refinement. The controller maintains
the accepted claim set from your assessments; you do not need to repeat that list. Explanations are
retained for inspection. Acceptance does not require prior independent validation.


You are investigating the supplied research dataset. Return one JSON object using
only this stage's response form. The service performs analyses; you choose the science.
For this task, a relative difference in outcome of 10% or greater is considered clinically significant.
Use your judgment about uncertainty and conclusions in light of this clinical significance threshold. Acceptance does not require
independent validation first. Explain your reasoning in narrative.

The ledger contains every registered claim, its current assessment, and all its available direct
evidence. References H1, H2, ... identify claims; R1, R2, ... identify evidence. Copy these short
references when needed. New proposals receive references automatically after this stage. A changed
comparison or reversed claim is a new proposal, optionally linked to an existing parent.
Proposal direction is the claim (+1 positive, -1 negative); anticipated_direction is your
expectation
of the raw exposed-minus-comparator contrast before seeing evidence (-1, 0 uncertain, +1).
initial_status is your assessment at registration. These initial judgments are recorded once.
If a proposal repeats an existing claim, the controller preserves that claim's current assessment;
use assessments to change a scientific conclusion.

For each claim in assessments_due, return one assessment with claim,
status (accept/reject/unresolved),
and investigation (active/deferred/closed). You may also reassess other claims. Omitted claims keep
their current assessment. Assess the original claim even when proposing a refinement or reversal.
By omitting evidence in an assessment, you assess all evidence displayed on that claim's card;
the controller attaches those references. To specify a subset or related evidence, provide evidence
with short R references; include the evidence listed in assessments_due for that claim.
An unchanged assessment or an investigation-only change can use evidence: [];
changing accept/reject/unresolved requires available evidence. Bookkeeping does not satisfy a due
evidence assessment.
For a refinement, parent identifies the earlier claim; omitted motivating_evidence attaches the
parent's displayed evidence. These automatic links record evidence supplied for your assessment
or refinement, not proof that you discussed or understood every result.

The controller maintains the accepted set from your assessments. Do not reconstruct it. Optional
research_notes replaces your persistent notebook; omit it to keep the existing notes. Use it for
plans or reasoning worth retaining. Latest stage narratives are also retained. All earlier numerical
evidence remains in the ledger. Do not repeat completed actions or old responses.
Omit unused fields.

Your action now: Propose scientifically useful new comparisons or refinements for later analysis.

For most dependencies, more negative scores mean stronger dependency. Negative-direction claims therefore predict exposed-minus-comparator raw differences below zero. Specifically, braf_v600e-positive lines are hypothesized to depend more on BRAF; kras_mutation-positive lines are hypothesized to depend more on KRAS and plausibly more on RIT1 as a related RAS-pathway node; egfr_amplification and erbb2_amplification are hypothesized to strengthen EGFR, ERBB2, and related signaling/trafficking dependencies. TP53 loss is expected to weaken MDM2 and RPL11 dependencies, so the expected raw difference is positive and the claim direction is +1. SMARCA4 loss is expected to strengthen SMARCA2 dependency, KEAP1 loss is expected to strengthen NFE2L2/NRF2 dependency, and MSI-high status is expected to strengthen WRN dependency. MYC amplification is used to probe transcriptional dependencies POLR2A, DHX9, and USP7; CDKN2A loss is used to probe mitotic dependency KIF18A. EGFR amplification is also tested for TMED10 trafficking/secretory dependence, and ERBB2 amplification for STAT3 dependence. These are discovery comparisons within supplied lung-lineage cell lines only; they are associations, not causal or generalizable claims. Later analyses should inspect whether signed estimates are both statistically credible (95% intervals away from zero and cell counts adequate) and clinically meaningful under the relative difference threshold, noting that a 10% difference corresponds to roughly 0.02-0.05 for many dependencies with means near -0.25, while broader outcomes such as SMARCA2, STAT3, WRN, NFE2L2, USP7, and MDM2 may require context-specific effect-size assessment.

Study instructions:
Investigate diverse, scientifically meaningful comparisons and use previous

throughout the run. Assess discoveries in this supplied dataset and use independent validation when

Register comparisons, anticipated directions, and initial assessments before requesting analyses.
The controller assigns claim references. For a changed claim, propose a new comparison and link
refinements to the earlier parent claim.
Clinical log_pfs_months is natural log progression-free survival in months, fully observed without
censoring. Dependency scores are continuous; more negative values mean stronger dependency.
Research signatures are constructed standardized assays in arbitrary units. Research markers D, E,
and F are constructed binary assays with no assigned gene, pathway, or clinical role.
A mean_difference is exposed minus comparator within eligibility and subgroup. An interaction
subtracts that comparison in the subgroup complement in the same eligible population.
Use your scientific judgment to assess the size, uncertainty, and importance of each effect
and decide which conclusions the evidence supports. Explain your reasoning in the narrative.

multiply them by direction again. For example, raw -0.4 with direction -1 is reported as +0.4.

comparison cell.

Each iteration has explore, analyze, appraise, and synthesize stages. Every stage may register
hypotheses for later analysis. Analyze selects up to 12 previously registered hypotheses.
Appraise assesses every new discovery result, records active/deferred/closed investigation, and may
request validation after considering those results. At most one new voluntary validation request
is allowed per iteration and ten per run. Cached requests reuse the same evidence. The evaluator
may also deliver scheduled validation during the run. Independent intervals account for the maximum
number of validation comparisons in the run. Results arrive before synthesis. Assess newly released
validation immediately in synthesis and explicitly reassess the original claim when its response
deadline appears in the context, even if you also investigate a refinement. The controller maintains
the accepted claim set from your assessments; you do not need to repeat that list. Explanations are
retained for inspection. Acceptance does not require prior independent validation.


You are investigating the supplied research dataset. Return one JSON object using
only this stage's response form. The service performs analyses; you choose the science.
For this task, a relative difference in outcome of 10% or greater is considered clinically significant.
Use your judgment about uncertainty and conclusions in light of this clinical significance threshold. Acceptance does not require
independent validation first. Explain your reasoning in narrative.

The ledger contains every registered claim, its current assessment, and all its available direct
evidence. References H1, H2, ... identify claims; R1, R2, ... identify evidence. Copy these short
references when needed. New proposals receive references automatically after this stage. A changed
comparison or reversed claim is a new proposal, optionally linked to an existing parent.

expectation
of the raw exposed-minus-comparator contrast before seeing evidence (-1, 0 uncertain, +1).
initial_status is your assessment at registration. These initial judgments are recorded once.
If a proposal repeats an existing claim, the controller preserves that claim's current assessment;

For each claim in assessments_due, return one assessment with claim,

An unchanged assessment or an investigation-only change can use evidence: [];

evidence assessment.
For a refinement, parent identifies the earlier claim; omitted motivating_evidence attaches the
parent's displayed evidence. These automatic links record evidence supplied for your assessment
or refinement, not proof that you discussed or understood every result.

The controller maintains the accepted set from your assessments. Do not reconstruct it. Optional
research_notes replaces your persistent notebook; omit it to keep the existing notes. Use it for
plans or reasoning worth retaining. Latest stage narratives are also retained. All earlier numerical
evidence remains in the ledger. Do not repeat completed actions or old responses.

record.narrative:
All estimates are already signed to the registered hypothesis direction, so a positive signed estimate supports a negative-direction dependency claim (raw exposed-minus-comparator more negative) and a negative signed estimate opposes it. H6, SMARCA4 loss versus dependency_SMARCA2, is an unambiguous accepted association in this dataset: signed mean_difference +0.784, 95% CI +0.765 to +0.803, n 412 vs 1588. This is both far outside zero and enormous relative to the SMARCA2 outcome distribution, supporting the synthetic-lethal prediction within the supplied data only. H8, MSI-high versus dependency_WRN, is likewise accepted: signed estimate +0.790, CI +0.760 to +0.819, n 130 vs 1870, indicating much stronger WRN dependency in MSI-high lines in this dataset. H7, KEAP1 loss versus dependency_NFE2L2, strongly rejects the registered negative-direction hypothesis. Its signed estimate is -0.796 with CI -0.816 to -0.776; for direction -1 this corresponds to a positive raw exposed-minus-comparator difference, meaning KEAP1-loss lines have weaker rather than stronger NFE2L2 dependency. I rejected the original claim and proposed a reversed-direction claim to characterize this opposite association.

Most other claims are null or underpowered. H1 was rejected because the signed estimate was negative/opposite and the most favorable upper signed value was only +0.012, well below a likely 10% relative threshold for dependency_BRAF. H10-H12 were rejected because favorable upper bounds were small relative to their outcome scales and CIs included substantial opposite values; the point estimates were near zero. H2, H4, H5, and H9 remain unresolved because their intervals cross zero while allowing clinically meaningful positive signed differences in some cases. H3 is the most scientifically useful borderline result: EGFR amplification versus dependency_EGFR has signed estimate +0.0252, close to 10% relative to the outcome scale, but CI lower bound is -0.00025, so it is not credible without validation. I requested validation for H3. Multiple-comparison risk is low for H6-H8 given how far intervals exclude zero, but H3 remains unresolved because it is near zero and was part of a 12-test discovery family.

Because critical reviewers must consider technical confounding, I registered follow-up comparisons restricted to the dominant Avana CRISPR library and, for H6, to higher screen quality (screen_roc_auc >= 0.95). These do not change the accepted associations unless the effect fails, but they probe whether the huge H6 and H8 effects could partly reflect screen-platform or quality differences. I also registered a research-marker null-style check for dependency_SMARCA2 to detect latent association structure. All conclusions remain dataset-specific associations, not causal or generalizable claims.

Each iteration has explore, analyze, appraise, and synthesize stages. Every stage may register
hypotheses for later analysis. Analyze selects up to 12 previously registered hypotheses.

is allowed per iteration and ten per run. Cached requests reuse the same evidence. The evaluator
may also deliver scheduled validation during the run. Independent intervals account for the maximum

deadline appears in the context, even if you also investigate a refinement. The controller maintains
the accepted claim set from your assessments; you do not need to repeat that list. Explanations are
retained for inspection. Acceptance does not require prior independent validation.

record.narrative:
The validation result for H3, EGFR amplification versus dependency_EGFR, does not support the original positive signed claim. The discovery estimate was only marginally favorable (+0.0252; CI approximately -0.0003 to +0.0507), and the independent validation estimate is opposite in sign (-0.0060) with an interval crossing zero and including clinically meaningful positive and negative values (-0.0497 to +0.0377). Because the independent interval still permits a meaningful positive effect, I do not treat this as definitive evidence against the association; however, the inconsistent and non-confirmatory validation evidence means H3 should not be accepted. I therefore assess H3 as unresolved and close the overall H3 investigation to prevent additional allocation to a low-confidence main effect unless a subgroup or refinement emerges separately.

I reassess H17 and accept it. H17 reverses the original KEAP1-loss/NFE2L2 hypothesis: the signed estimate is +0.796 (CI +0.776 to +0.816) with n = 393 versus 1607. Since H17 has direction +1, this corresponds to a raw exposed-minus-comparator difference above zero, meaning KEAP1-loss lines have weaker, not stronger, NFE2L2 dependency in the supplied dataset. This is a very strong dataset-specific association, though unexpected relative to the usual KEAP1/NFE2L2 synthetic-lethal intuition. It should not be interpreted as causal or generalizable, and it deserves technical robustness checks because the outcome mean is near zero and the direction is opposite to the prior.

H6 and H8 remain the strongest accepted findings: SMARCA4 loss is associated with much stronger SMARCA2 dependency, and MSI-high status is associated with much stronger WRN dependency. I propose quality-restricted and platform-restricted versions of these accepted findings, plus subtype-interaction analyses, to determine whether they persist across CRISPR screen quality and lineage subtype. I also register constructed research-marker null-style checks to probe whether latent marker effects contribute to the observed large dependency associations. The immediate priority is robustness of H6, H8, and especially H17, rather than pursuing H3 further.

Use independent validation when useful and distinguish findings in this dataset from claims about causality or generalizability.
Each iteration proceeds through explore (propose comparisons), analyze (request tests), appraise (assess the resulting discovery evidence and optionally request validation), and synthesize (assess validation and update conclusions and plans).

Study instructions:
Investigate diverse, scientifically meaningful comparisons and use previous
results to allocate further investigation. Broad exploration and focused follow-up are both useful
throughout the run. Assess discoveries in this supplied dataset and use independent validation when
useful. Biological interpretation and generalizability may remain uncertain.

Register comparisons, anticipated directions, and initial assessments before requesting analyses.
The controller assigns claim references. For a changed claim, propose a new comparison and link
refinements to the earlier parent claim.
Clinical log_pfs_months is natural log progression-free survival in months, fully observed without
censoring. Dependency scores are continuous; more negative values mean stronger dependency.
Research signatures are constructed standardized assays in arbitrary units. Research markers D, E,
and F are constructed binary assays with no assigned gene, pathway, or clinical role.
A mean_difference is exposed minus comparator within eligibility and subgroup. An interaction
subtracts that comparison in the subgroup complement in the same eligible population.
Use your scientific judgment to assess the size, uncertainty, and importance of each effect
and decide which conclusions the evidence supports. Explain your reasoning in the narrative.
Returned estimates and intervals are ALREADY SIGNED to the indicated hypothesis direction. Do not
multiply them by direction again. For example, raw -0.4 with direction -1 is reported as +0.4.
Discovery analyses use 95% Welch intervals and need at least 20 observations in every
comparison cell.

Each iteration has explore, analyze, appraise, and synthesize stages. Every stage may register
hypotheses for later analysis. Analyze selects up to 12 previously registered hypotheses.
Appraise assesses every new discovery result, records active/deferred/closed investigation, and may
request validation after considering those results. At most one new voluntary validation request
is allowed per iteration and ten per run. Cached requests reuse the same evidence. The evaluator
may also deliver scheduled validation during the run. Independent intervals account for the maximum
number of validation comparisons in the run. Results arrive before synthesis. Assess newly released
validation immediately in synthesis and explicitly reassess the original claim when its response
deadline appears in the context, even if you also investigate a refinement. The controller maintains
the accepted claim set from your assessments; you do not need to repeat that list. Explanations are
retained for inspection. Acceptance does not require prior independent validation.


You are investigating the supplied research dataset. Return one JSON object using
only this stage's response form. The service performs analyses; you choose the science.
For this task, a relative difference in outcome of 10% or greater is considered clinically significant.
Use your judgment about uncertainty and conclusions in light of this clinical significance threshold. Acceptance does not require
independent validation first. Explain your reasoning in narrative.

The ledger contains every registered claim, its current assessment, and all its available direct
evidence. References H1, H2, ... identify claims; R1, R2, ... identify evidence. Copy these short
references when needed. New proposals receive references automatically after this stage. A changed
comparison or reversed claim is a new proposal, optionally linked to an existing parent.
Proposal direction is the claim (+1 positive, -1 negative); anticipated_direction is your
expectation
of the raw exposed-minus-comparator contrast before seeing evidence (-1, 0 uncertain, +1).
initial_status is your assessment at registration. These initial judgments are recorded once.
If a proposal repeats an existing claim, the controller preserves that claim's current assessment;
use assessments to change a scientific conclusion.

For each claim in assessments_due, return one assessment with claim,
status (accept/reject/unresolved),
and investigation (active/deferred/closed). You may also reassess other claims. Omitted claims keep
their current assessment. Assess the original claim even when proposing a refinement or reversal.
By omitting evidence in an assessment, you assess all evidence displayed on that claim's card;
the controller attaches those references. To specify a subset or related evidence, provide evidence
with short R references; include the evidence listed in assessments_due for that claim.
An unchanged assessment or an investigation-only change can use evidence: [];
changing accept/reject/unresolved requires available evidence. Bookkeeping does not satisfy a due
evidence assessment.
For a refinement, parent identifies the earlier claim; omitted motivating_evidence attaches the
parent's displayed evidence. These automatic links record evidence supplied for your assessment
or refinement, not proof that you discussed or understood every result.

The controller maintains the accepted set from your assessments. Do not reconstruct it. Optional
research_notes replaces your persistent notebook; omit it to keep the existing notes. Use it for
plans or reasoning worth retaining. Latest stage narratives are also retained. All earlier numerical
evidence remains in the ledger. Do not repeat completed actions or old responses.
Omit unused fields.

Your action now: Propose scientifically useful new comparisons or refinements for later analysis.

record.narrative:
The next round should separate robust accepted dataset associations from technical or biologic modifiers. For dependency_SMARCA2, dependency_WRN, and dependency_NFE2L2, the accepted effects are very large in the full lung-lineage dataset, but critical reviewers should still ask whether they persist in high-Cas9 screens, because Cas9 activity is an orthogonal screen-quality variable not covered by the Avana-library or screen_roc_auc restrictions. These are robustness tests, not new biology claims. I also registered modifier interactions: ARID1A loss may alter SMARCA2 dependency in SMARCA4-mutant backgrounds, and TP53 loss may alter the unexpectedly weaker NFE2L2 dependency associated with KEAP1 loss. For interactions, positive signed estimates indicate a stronger accepted-direction effect in the subgroup relative to its complement; I kept anticipated directions uncertain where no firm prior exists.

I added focused subgroup/broad biological follow-ups. EGFR amplification had an unresolved main effect with inconsistent validation, so testing EGFR amplification specifically in adenocarcinoma could reveal a subtype-specific effect rather than continuing the closed overall claim. I also registered biologically motivated predictor hypotheses for outcomes with unexplored or incomplete coverage: MYC amplification may strengthen ribosome-biogenesis-associated RPL11 dependency; PIK3CA mutation may strengthen STAT3 dependency through growth-pathway signaling; RB1 loss may strengthen KIF18A dependency because RB1 loss is associated with increased cell-cycle/mitotic pressure. All new negative-direction dependency claims expect stronger dependency, i.e. raw exposed-minus-comparator scores below zero, which will be returned as positive signed estimates. The 10% relative threshold is context dependent: outcomes centered near -0.25 to -0.28 correspond roughly to 0.025-0.028 absolute difference, while the accepted huge effects around 0.8 are far beyond any reasonable clinical threshold. All conclusions remain associations in this supplied dataset, not causal claims or generalized predictions.

Iteration 2/25, stage analyze, attempt 1.
Research goal: investigate which measured predictors and subgroups are associated with scientifically meaningful differences in dependency_BRAF (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_DHX9 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_EGFR (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_ERBB2 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_KIF18A (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_KRAS (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_MDM2 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_NFE2L2 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_POLR2A (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_RIT1 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_RPL11 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_SMARCA2 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_STAT3 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_TMED10 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_USP7 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_WRN (CRISPR dependency score). Use the supplied dataset to discover and follow up comparisons, assess effect sizes and uncertainty, and decide which conclusions the evidence supports. Use independent validation when useful and distinguish findings in this dataset from claims about causality or generalizability.
Each iteration proceeds through explore (propose comparisons), analyze (request tests), appraise (assess the resulting discovery evidence and optionally request validation), and synthesize (assess validation and update conclusions and plans).

Study instructions:
Investigate diverse, scientifically meaningful comparisons and use previous
results to allocate further investigation. Broad exploration and focused follow-up are both useful
throughout the run. Assess discoveries in this supplied dataset and use independent validation when
useful. Biological interpretation and generalizability may remain uncertain.

Register comparisons, anticipated directions, and initial assessments before requesting analyses.
The controller assigns claim references. For a changed claim, propose a new comparison and link
refinements to the earlier parent claim.
Clinical log_pfs_months is natural log progression-free survival in months, fully observed without
censoring. Dependency scores are continuous; more negative values mean stronger dependency.
Research signatures are constructed standardized assays in arbitrary units. Research markers D, E,
and F are constructed binary assays with no assigned gene, pathway, or clinical role.
A mean_difference is exposed minus comparator within eligibility and subgroup. An interaction
subtracts that comparison in the subgroup complement in the same eligible population.
Use your scientific judgment to assess the size, uncertainty, and importance of each effect
and decide which conclusions the evidence supports. Explain your reasoning in the narrative.
Returned estimates and intervals are ALREADY SIGNED to the indicated hypothesis direction. Do not
multiply them by direction again. For example, raw -0.4 with direction -1 is reported as +0.4.
Discovery analyses use 95% Welch intervals and need at least 20 observations in every
comparison cell.

Each iteration has explore, analyze, appraise, and synthesize stages. Every stage may register
hypotheses for later analysis. Analyze selects up to 12 previously registered hypotheses.
Appraise assesses every new discovery result, records active/deferred/closed investigation, and may
request validation after considering those results. At most one new voluntary validation request
is allowed per iteration and ten per run. Cached requests reuse the same evidence. The evaluator
may also deliver scheduled validation during the run. Independent intervals account for the maximum
number of validation comparisons in the run. Results arrive before synthesis. Assess newly released
validation immediately in synthesis and explicitly reassess the original claim when its response
deadline appears in the context, even if you also investigate a refinement. The controller maintains
the accepted claim set from your assessments; you do not need to repeat that list. Explanations are
retained for inspection. Acceptance does not require prior independent validation.


You are investigating the supplied research dataset. Return one JSON object using
only this stage's response form. The service performs analyses; you choose the science.
For this task, a relative difference in outcome of 10% or greater is considered clinically significant.
Use your judgment about uncertainty and conclusions in light of this clinical significance threshold. Acceptance does not require
independent validation first. Explain your reasoning in narrative.

The ledger contains every registered claim, its current assessment, and all its available direct
evidence. References H1, H2, ... identify claims; R1, R2, ... identify evidence. Copy these short
references when needed. New proposals receive references automatically after this stage. A changed
comparison or reversed claim is a new proposal, optionally linked to an existing parent.
Proposal direction is the claim (+1 positive, -1 negative); anticipated_direction is your
expectation
of the raw exposed-minus-comparator contrast before seeing evidence (-1, 0 uncertain, +1).
initial_status is your assessment at registration. These initial judgments are recorded once.
If a proposal repeats an existing claim, the controller preserves that claim's current assessment;
use assessments to change a scientific conclusion.

For each claim in assessments_due, return one assessment with claim,
status (accept/reject/unresolved),
and investigation (active/deferred/closed). You may also reassess other claims. Omitted claims keep
their current assessment. Assess the original claim even when proposing a refinement or reversal.
By omitting evidence in an assessment, you assess all evidence displayed on that claim's card;
the controller attaches those references. To specify a subset or related evidence, provide evidence
with short R references; include the evidence listed in assessments_due for that claim.
An unchanged assessment or an investigation-only change can use evidence: [];
changing accept/reject/unresolved requires available evidence. Bookkeeping does not satisfy a due
evidence assessment.
For a refinement, parent identifies the earlier claim; omitted motivating_evidence attaches the
parent's displayed evidence. These automatic links record evidence supplied for your assessment
or refinement, not proof that you discussed or understood every result.

The controller maintains the accepted set from your assessments. Do not reconstruct it. Optional
research_notes replaces your persistent notebook; omit it to keep the existing notes. Use it for
plans or reasoning worth retaining. Latest stage narratives are also retained. All earlier numerical
evidence remains in the ledger. Do not repeat completed actions or old responses.
Omit unused fields.

Your action now: Select up to 12 existing claim references in run_analyses. This requests analyses now; previously tested comparisons reuse their data and give no new sample. New results enter the ledger after this form is accepted and are assessed in appraise. Any assessment in this form must use evidence already in the supplied ledger.

record.narrative:
The new restricted analyses strongly support the robustness of the three major dataset associations already accepted. For dependency_SMARCA2, restricting to the dominant Avana library gives signed estimate +0.781 (95% CI +0.760 to +0.802; n 351 vs 1414), and restricting to higher screen quality (screen_roc_auc >= 0.95) gives +0.790 (+0.765 to +0.816; n 243 vs 918). For dependency_WRN, Avana restriction gives +0.794 (+0.764 to +0.825; n 120 vs 1645), and high screen quality gives +0.795 (+0.758 to +0.832; n 85 vs 1076). For dependency_NFE2L2, Avana restriction gives +0.796 (+0.774 to +0.818; n 353 vs 1412), and high screen quality gives +0.790 (+0.763 to +0.816; n 235 vs 926). These are not independent external confirmations, but they are same-dataset robustness checks: the huge signed effects remain essentially unchanged when dominant library or lower screen quality is excluded. I accept them as completed robustness checks and close these technical robustness investigations, while leaving the broader accepted claims active because other modifiers and null controls remain to be assessed.

The newly tested small-effect hypotheses mostly support nulls or inconclusive effects. H13, CDKN2A loss versus dependency_KIF18A, has signed estimate -0.0133 (CI -0.0332 to +0.0065); the entire signed interval is below the approximately 0.025-0.026 absolute threshold corresponding to a 10% relative difference for KIF18A-scale outcomes. It is therefore rejected and closed. H36, MYC amplification versus dependency_RPL11, has signed estimate -0.0125 (CI -0.0339 to +0.0090), also far below clinical significance and opposite in sign, so it is rejected and closed. H38, RB1 loss versus dependency_KIF18A, has point estimate +0.0082 (CI -0.0193 to +0.0357); it is not credible because the point is near null and the interval crosses both null and meaningful positive values, so I leave it unresolved and deferred rather than continue to prioritize it now.

H15, ERBB2 amplification versus dependency_STAT3, is the most useful borderline new result. Its signed estimate is +0.0222 (CI -0.0147 to +0.0592; n 162 vs 1838). This is near the 10% relative threshold for dependency_STAT3 but imprecise. Because H15 is biologically plausible, new, and eligible, I request independent validation for H15. Validation is preferable to spending another discovery test on this borderline effect because it could determine whether the result is a confirmatory dataset association or another low-confidence null.

The interaction analyses are inconclusive. H33, ARID1A loss modifying the SMARCA4-loss effect on dependency_SMARCA2, has positive signed interaction +0.0373 (CI -0.0148 to +0.0894). This suggests a stronger SMARCA4-loss association in ARID1A-positive lines, but the small ARID1A-positive SMARCA4-loss cell (n=76) gives wide uncertainty, and the point is near/below a 10% relative difference relative to SMARCA2 outcome scale. I keep it active and register a refinement that estimates the SMARCA4-loss effect directly within ARID1A-positive lines. H34, TP53 loss modifying the KEAP1-loss/NFE2L2 association, is +0.0176 (CI -0.0340 to +0.0693); this is unresolved but low priority and deferred.

I also registered subgroup refinements for KRAS and ERBB2 in adenocarcinoma. These are reasonable because oncogene addiction may be subtype-specific and the main effects were unresolved, but they are follow-up hypotheses rather than current accepted claims. All conclusions remain associations in the supplied lung-lineage CRISPR dataset and are not causal or generalized.

Study instructions:

results to allocate further investigation. Broad exploration and focused follow-up are both useful
throughout the run. Assess discoveries in this supplied dataset and use independent validation when
useful. Biological interpretation and generalizability may remain uncertain.

Register comparisons, anticipated directions, and initial assessments before requesting analyses.
The controller assigns claim references. For a changed claim, propose a new comparison and link
refinements to the earlier parent claim.
Clinical log_pfs_months is natural log progression-free survival in months, fully observed without
censoring. Dependency scores are continuous; more negative values mean stronger dependency.
Research signatures are constructed standardized assays in arbitrary units. Research markers D, E,
and F are constructed binary assays with no assigned gene, pathway, or clinical role.
A mean_difference is exposed minus comparator within eligibility and subgroup. An interaction
subtracts that comparison in the subgroup complement in the same eligible population.
Use your scientific judgment to assess the size, uncertainty, and importance of each effect
and decide which conclusions the evidence supports. Explain your reasoning in the narrative.

multiply them by direction again. For example, raw -0.4 with direction -1 is reported as +0.4.

comparison cell.

hypotheses for later analysis. Analyze selects up to 12 previously registered hypotheses.
Appraise assesses every new discovery result, records active/deferred/closed investigation, and may
request validation after considering those results. At most one new voluntary validation request
is allowed per iteration and ten per run. Cached requests reuse the same evidence. The evaluator
may also deliver scheduled validation during the run. Independent intervals account for the maximum
number of validation comparisons in the run. Results arrive before synthesis. Assess newly released
validation immediately in synthesis and explicitly reassess the original claim when its response
deadline appears in the context, even if you also investigate a refinement. The controller maintains
the accepted claim set from your assessments; you do not need to repeat that list. Explanations are
retained for inspection. Acceptance does not require prior independent validation.

For this task, a relative difference in outcome of 10% or greater is considered clinically significant.

independent validation first. Explain your reasoning in narrative.

The ledger contains every registered claim, its current assessment, and all its available direct

record.narrative: The independent validation for H15, ERBB2 amplification versus dependency_STAT3, gives signed mean_difference +0.0243 with independent interval -0.0291 to +0.0776. This is very close to the discovery signed estimate +0.0222 and is not opposite in sign, unlike the H3 EGFR validation pattern. That consistency argues against treating the original discovery estimate as a one-sided fluke. However, the validation interval is wide because the independent validation comparison uses a stricter alpha, it crosses zero, and the lower tail includes a clinically relevant opposite-direction difference. Moreover, the point estimate itself is below the task's 10% relative-effect threshold for an outcome with mean around -0.28: a 10% difference is roughly 0.028 absolute, whereas the validation point is about 0.024 and the discovery point about 0.022. The data therefore support a suggestive small positive association between ERBB2 amplification and stronger STAT3 dependency, but not enough to accept the overall association as clinically meaningful under the stated threshold. I do not reject H15 because the two estimates are concordant and the intervals contain meaningful positive effects, but I close the overall H15 investigation because further same-data validation would not be as informative as testing whether the effect is diluted or enriched in a biologically relevant subtype. The registered adenocarcinoma-specific refinement is a conservative follow-up: ERBB2 signaling may be enriched in adenocarcinoma, so subtype restriction could reveal a larger clinically meaningful association. If that subgroup estimate remains near or below the 10% threshold and crosses zero, it would further argue that the ERBB2-STAT3 association is not robust at a meaningful magnitude. All conclusions remain dataset-specific associations, not causal claims or generalizable predictions.

record.narrative: The current priority is to turn the three large accepted dataset associations into more interpretable, robust, and specific findings rather than only adding new predictors. First, I registered direct estimates of the accepted effects in non-Avana CRISPR screens. We already accepted that the SMARCA4-loss/SMARCA2, MSI-high/WRN, and KEAP1-loss/NFE2L2 associations persist in the dominant Avana library and in higher-ROC screens. Testing the same contrasts in non-Avana libraries is an important orthogonal technical check: if the effects remain large and correctly signed there, they are less likely to be an artifact of the dominant library. Because the non-Avana subset is smaller, I kept these as direct comparisons with adequate expected cell counts rather than over-restricting by multiple quality filters. Second, I registered marker-null specificity interactions. The research markers D, E, and F are stated to have no assigned biological role, so a biologically credible dependency association should not be strongly modified by the corresponding marker. These interaction tests ask whether the accepted effects are diluted or concentrated in marker-positive lines. Near-zero interactions would increase confidence that the huge accepted effects are not driven by latent marker-positive structure; large marker interactions would be a warning about dataset-specific confounding and would need reconsideration. Third, I added two focused biological probes for under-tested predictor-outcome pairs. TP53 loss versus USP7 dependency is biologically motivated because USP7 participates in the MDM2-p53 axis, so TP53-deficient lines may depend less on USP7; I therefore registered a positive signed direction expecting weaker USP7 dependency in TP53-loss lines. BRAF V600E versus RIT1 dependency is plausible because RIT1 is a RAS/MAPK-adjacent GTPase and BRAF-mutant lines may use alternate MAPK-pathway dependencies; I registered a negative direction expecting stronger RIT1 dependency. All proposals are still discovery associations within the supplied lung-lineage dataset, not causal claims or external generalizability claims.

Testing the same contrasts in non-Avana libraries is an important orthogonal technical check: if the effects remain large and correctly signed there, they are less likely to be an artifact of the dominant library. Because the non-Avana subset is smaller, I kept these as direct comparisons with adequate expected cell counts rather than over-restricting by multiple quality filters. Second, I registered marker-null specificity interactions. The research markers D, E, and F are stated to have no assigned biological role, so a biologically credible dependency association should not be strongly modified by the corresponding marker. These interaction tests ask whether the accepted effects are diluted or concentrated in marker-positive lines. Near-zero interactions would increase confidence that the huge accepted effects are not driven by latent marker-positive structure; large marker interactions would be a warning about dataset-specific confounding and would need reconsideration. Third, I added two focused biological probes for under-tested predictor-outcome pairs. TP53 loss versus USP7 dependency is biologically motivated because USP7 participates in the MDM2-p53 axis, so TP53-deficient lines may depend less on USP7; I therefore registered a positive signed direction expecting weaker USP7 dependency in TP53-loss lines. BRAF V600E versus RIT1 dependency is plausible because RIT1 is a RAS/MAPK-adjacent GTPase and BRAF-mutant lines may use alternate MAPK-pathway dependencies; I registered a negative direction expecting stronger RIT1 dependency. Use independent validation when useful and distinguish findings in this dataset from claims about causality or generalizability.
Each iteration proceeds through explore (propose comparisons), analyze (request tests), appraise (assess the resulting discovery evidence and optionally request validation), and synthesize (assess validation and update conclusions and plans).

Study instructions:
Investigate diverse, scientifically meaningful comparisons and use previous
results to allocate further investigation. Broad exploration and focused follow-up are both useful
throughout the run. Assess discoveries in this supplied dataset and use independent validation when
useful. Biological interpretation and generalizability may remain uncertain.

Register comparisons, anticipated directions, and initial assessments before requesting analyses.
The controller assigns claim references. For a changed claim, propose a new comparison and link
refinements to the earlier parent claim.
Clinical log_pfs_months is natural log progression-free survival in months, fully observed without
censoring. Dependency scores are continuous; more negative values mean stronger dependency.
Research signatures are constructed standardized assays in arbitrary units. Research markers D, E,
and F are constructed binary assays with no assigned gene, pathway, or clinical role.
A mean_difference is exposed minus comparator within eligibility and subgroup. An interaction
subtracts that comparison in the subgroup complement in the same eligible population.
Use your scientific judgment to assess the size, uncertainty, and importance of each effect
and decide which conclusions the evidence supports. Explain your reasoning in the narrative.
Returned estimates and intervals are ALREADY SIGNED to the indicated hypothesis direction. Do not
multiply them by direction again. For example, raw -0.4 with direction -1 is reported as +0.4.
Discovery analyses use 95% Welch intervals and need at least 20 observations in every
comparison cell.

Each iteration has explore, analyze, appraise, and synthesize stages. Every stage may register
hypotheses for later analysis. Analyze selects up to 12 previously registered hypotheses.
Appraise assesses every new discovery result, records active/deferred/closed investigation, and may
request validation after considering those results. At most one new voluntary validation request
is allowed per iteration and ten per run. Cached requests reuse the same evidence. The evaluator
may also deliver scheduled validation during the run. Independent intervals account for the maximum
number of validation comparisons in the run. Results arrive before synthesis. Assess newly released
validation immediately in synthesis and explicitly reassess the original claim when its response
deadline appears in the context, even if you also investigate a refinement. The controller maintains
the accepted claim set from your assessments; you do not need to repeat that list. Explanations are
retained for inspection. Acceptance does not require prior independent validation.


You are investigating the supplied research dataset. Return one JSON object using
only this stage's response form. The service performs analyses; you choose the science.
For this task, a relative difference in outcome of 10% or greater is considered clinically significant.
Use your judgment about uncertainty and conclusions in light of this clinical significance threshold. Acceptance does not require
independent validation first. Explain your reasoning in narrative.

The ledger contains every registered claim, its current assessment, and all its available direct
evidence. References H1, H2, ... identify claims; R1, R2, ... identify evidence. Copy these short
references when needed. New proposals receive references automatically after this stage. A changed
comparison or reversed claim is a new proposal, optionally linked to an existing parent.
Proposal direction is the claim (+1 positive, -1 negative); anticipated_direction is your
expectation
of the raw exposed-minus-comparator contrast before seeing evidence (-1, 0 uncertain, +1).
initial_status is your assessment at registration. These initial judgments are recorded once.
If a proposal repeats an existing claim, the controller preserves that claim's current assessment;
use assessments to change a scientific conclusion.

For each claim in assessments_due, return one assessment with claim,
status (accept/reject/unresolved),
and investigation (active/deferred/closed). You may also reassess other claims. Omitted claims keep
their current assessment. Assess the original claim even when proposing a refinement or reversal.
By omitting evidence in an assessment, you assess all evidence displayed on that claim's card;
the controller attaches those references. To specify a subset or related evidence, provide evidence
with short R references; include the evidence listed in assessments_due for that claim.
An unchanged assessment or an investigation-only change can use evidence: [];
changing accept/reject/unresolved requires available evidence. Bookkeeping does not satisfy a due
evidence assessment.
For a refinement, parent identifies the earlier claim; omitted motivating_evidence attaches the
parent's displayed evidence. These automatic links record evidence supplied for your assessment
or refinement, not proof that you discussed or understood every result.

The controller maintains the accepted set from your assessments. Do not reconstruct it. Optional
research_notes replaces your persistent notebook; omit it to keep the existing notes. Use it for
plans or reasoning worth retaining. Latest stage narratives are also retained. All earlier numerical
evidence remains in the ledger. Do not repeat completed actions or old responses.
Omit unused fields.

Your action now: Assess the newly delivered discovery evidence. Optionally set validate to one eligible claim reference for independent validation; omit it for no request. The controller attaches the discovery result. Validation arrives after this stage.

record.narrative:
The new results further strengthen the three large accepted dataset associations. In high-Cas9 screens, SMARCA4-loss versus dependency_SMARCA2 is +0.788 (CI +0.756 to +0.820), MSI-high versus dependency_WRN is +0.776 (CI +0.728 to +0.824), and KEAP1-loss versus dependency_NFE2L2 is +0.800 (CI +0.769 to +0.831). In non-Avana screens, SMARCA4-loss versus SMARCA2 is +0.801 (CI +0.748 to +0.853) and KEAP1-loss versus NFE2L2 is +0.794 (CI +0.746 to +0.842). These are not independent external validations, but they are informative same-dataset technical robustness checks: the huge signed effects remain far above clinical thresholds when dominant library or high Cas9 activity subsets are used. I accept and close these restricted robustness claims.

The adenocarcinoma interaction tests mostly do not show clinically meaningful modification of the accepted effects. H25 has signed estimate -0.028 (CI -0.076 to +0.020); the maximum positive claim-direction magnitude is below the approximate 0.041 threshold for a 10% effect on dependency_SMARCA2, so I reject it. H26 and H27 are near null (-0.021 and -0.012), and their intervals include some support above their approximate 0.030 absolute thresholds, so I do not reject them outright, but I close them because they are low-priority specificity checks and there is no clear evidence that adenocarcinoma subtype drives the accepted effects.

The research-marker interaction tests are reassuringly small: H46 +0.008, H47 -0.005, and H48 +0.007. However, their 95% intervals still include some marker-specific differences above a 10%-scale threshold, so I leave these interaction claims unresolved but closed as direct specificity evidence rather than continue validation. I registered a companion direct control for marker F against dependency_NFE2L2 because the existing interaction companion lacks the corresponding direct marker-outcome control.

H42, ERBB2 amplification versus dependency_STAT3 within adenocarcinoma, gives signed estimate +0.021 (CI -0.024 to +0.066). The point estimate is below the approximately 0.028 absolute threshold corresponding to a 10% effect for STAT3-scale outcomes, and the interval crosses null. This does not support clinically meaningful enrichment in adenocarcinoma. Since H15 overall was also borderline and already independently validated without reaching the threshold, I leave H42 unresolved but closed and do not request validation. I omitted a validation request because the huge accepted effects do not need it and the remaining borderline subgroup effect is unlikely to become interpretable with a wider independent interval. All conclusions remain associations within the supplied lung-lineage dataset, not causal claims or generalizable predictions.

Each iteration proceeds through explore (propose comparisons), analyze (request tests), appraise (assess the resulting discovery evidence and optionally request validation), and synthesize (assess validation and update conclusions and plans).

Study instructions:
Investigate diverse, scientifically meaningful comparisons and use previous
results to allocate further investigation. Broad exploration and focused follow-up are both useful
throughout the run. Assess discoveries in this supplied dataset and use independent validation when
useful. Biological interpretation and generalizability may remain uncertain.

Register comparisons, anticipated directions, and initial assessments before requesting analyses.
The controller assigns claim references. For a changed claim, propose a new comparison and link
refinements to the earlier parent claim.
Clinical log_pfs_months is natural log progression-free survival in months, fully observed without
censoring. Dependency scores are continuous; more negative values mean stronger dependency.
Research signatures are constructed standardized assays in arbitrary units. Research markers D, E,
and F are constructed binary assays with no assigned gene, pathway, or clinical role.
A mean_difference is exposed minus comparator within eligibility and subgroup. An interaction
subtracts that comparison in the subgroup complement in the same eligible population.
Use your scientific judgment to assess the size, uncertainty, and importance of each effect
and decide which conclusions the evidence supports. Explain your reasoning in the narrative.
Returned estimates and intervals are ALREADY SIGNED to the indicated hypothesis direction. Do not
multiply them by direction again. For example, raw -0.4 with direction -1 is reported as +0.4.
Discovery analyses use 95% Welch intervals and need at least 20 observations in every
comparison cell.

Each iteration has explore, analyze, appraise, and synthesize stages. Every stage may register
hypotheses for later analysis. Analyze selects up to 12 previously registered hypotheses.
Appraise assesses every new discovery result, records active/deferred/closed investigation, and may
request validation after considering those results. At most one new voluntary validation request
is allowed per iteration and ten per run. Cached requests reuse the same evidence. The evaluator
may also deliver scheduled validation during the run. Independent intervals account for the maximum
number of validation comparisons in the run. Results arrive before synthesis. Assess newly released
validation immediately in synthesis and explicitly reassess the original claim when its response
deadline appears in the context, even if you also investigate a refinement. The controller maintains
the accepted claim set from your assessments; you do not need to repeat that list. Explanations are
retained for inspection. Acceptance does not require prior independent validation.


You are investigating the supplied research dataset. Return one JSON object using
only this stage's response form. The service performs analyses; you choose the science.
For this task, a relative difference in outcome of 10% or greater is considered clinically significant.
Use your judgment about uncertainty and conclusions in light of this clinical significance threshold. Acceptance does not require
independent validation first. Explain your reasoning in narrative.

The ledger contains every registered claim, its current assessment, and all its available direct
evidence. References H1, H2, ... identify claims; R1, R2, ... identify evidence. Copy these short
references when needed. New proposals receive references automatically after this stage. A changed
comparison or reversed claim is a new proposal, optionally linked to an existing parent.
Proposal direction is the claim (+1 positive, -1 negative); anticipated_direction is your
expectation
of the raw exposed-minus-comparator contrast before seeing evidence (-1, 0 uncertain, +1).
initial_status is your assessment at registration. These initial judgments are recorded once.
If a proposal repeats an existing claim, the controller preserves that claim's current assessment;
use assessments to change a scientific conclusion.

For each claim in assessments_due, return one assessment with claim,
status (accept/reject/unresolved),
and investigation (active/deferred/closed). You may also reassess other claims. Omitted claims keep
their current assessment. Assess the original claim even when proposing a refinement or reversal.
By omitting evidence in an assessment, you assess all evidence displayed on that claim's card;
the controller attaches those references. To specify a subset or related evidence, provide evidence
with short R references; include the evidence listed in assessments_due for that claim.
An unchanged assessment or an investigation-only change can use evidence: [];
changing accept/reject/unresolved requires available evidence. Bookkeeping does not satisfy a due
evidence assessment.
For a refinement, parent identifies the earlier claim; omitted motivating_evidence attaches the
parent's displayed evidence. These automatic links record evidence supplied for your assessment
or refinement, not proof that you discussed or understood every result.

The controller maintains the accepted set from your assessments. Do not reconstruct it. Optional
research_notes replaces your persistent notebook; omit it to keep the existing notes. Use it for
plans or reasoning worth retaining. Latest stage narratives are also retained. All earlier numerical
evidence remains in the ledger. Do not repeat completed actions or old responses.
Omit unused fields.

Your action now: Assess new validation and any response deadlines listed below. Explain what you conclude and what to investigate next. Accepted claims update automatically.

record.narrative:
The newly released independent validation for H24 is decisive. In high screen-quality screens, the KEAP1-loss association with weaker dependency_NFE2L2 has signed estimate +0.799 with independent 95% interval +0.759 to +0.839, using the stricter validation alpha. This is orders of magnitude larger than any plausible 10%-relative threshold for NFE2L2-scale outcomes and lies far from both the null and any meaningful opposite-direction effect. Thus H24 is accepted and closed: the KEAP1-loss effect is robust even when restricted to high-quality screens, and the independent validation interval supports the same huge positive signed association. Because this validates the high-ROC restricted contrast, I also close the broader accepted main effect H17; the original huge association remains accepted and now has supportive independent evidence, but further investigation of this main effect would be less informative than testing new predictors or specificity probes.

For the overdue response deadline on H3, the independent validation changes the conclusion from unresolved to reject. Discovery had signed estimate +0.0252 with interval -0.0003 to +0.0507, barely near the approximately 0.025 absolute threshold for a 10% effect on dependency_EGFR and still including null. Independent validation gave signed estimate -0.0060 with interval -0.0497 to +0.0377, i.e., a small opposite-direction point estimate and wide uncertainty. The combination does not support a clinically meaningful EGFR-amplification association with stronger dependency_EGFR. I therefore reject and close H3 and also close the adenocarcinoma refinement H35 as low priority, because the main EGFR-amplification effect is not supported.

The three major accepted dataset associations are now sufficiently characterized for the same dataset. SMARCA4-loss versus stronger dependency_SMARCA2 remains accepted, with huge direct estimates and robustness across Avana, non-Avana, high screen-quality, and high-Cas9 subsets. MSI-high versus stronger dependency_WRN remains accepted, with huge direct estimates and robustness across high ROC and high Cas9 subsets; the non-Avana WRN cell was expected sparse and is not needed for closure. KEAP1-loss versus weaker dependency_NFE2L2 remains accepted, with robustness across library, screen quality, Cas9 activity, non-Avana screens, and now independent validation of the high-ROC restricted estimate. I close the main accepted effects H6, H8, and H17 to focus future analysis on unresolved predictors and specificity probes rather than repeatedly validating effects that are already far above the clinical threshold.

I also close H33, the ARID1A-loss interaction modifying the SMARCA4-loss effect on dependency_SMARCA2, because the direct ARID1A-positive probe H39 is the better next test and the interaction estimate +0.037 was imprecise and near the SMARCA2-scale 10% threshold. The current best next set of discovery analyses is the active unrun probe set: EGFR amplification versus TMED10 dependency, TP53 loss versus RPL11 dependency, marker-null direct controls, PIK3CA mutation versus STAT3 dependency, SMARCA4-loss effect restricted to ARID1A-loss lines, KRAS and ERBB2 subtype probes, TP53 loss versus USP7 dependency, BRAF V600E versus RIT1 dependency, and marker F versus NFE2L2 dependency. All conclusions remain associations within the supplied lung-lineage CRISPR dataset, not causal claims or claims of external generalizability.

Use the supplied dataset to discover and follow up comparisons, assess effect sizes and uncertainty, and decide which conclusions the evidence supports. Use independent validation when useful and distinguish findings in this dataset from claims about causality or generalizability.
Each iteration proceeds through explore (propose comparisons), analyze (request tests), appraise (assess the resulting discovery evidence and optionally request validation), and synthesize (assess validation and update conclusions and plans).

Study instructions:
Investigate diverse, scientifically meaningful comparisons and use previous
results to allocate further investigation. Broad exploration and focused follow-up are both useful
throughout the run. Assess discoveries in this supplied dataset and use independent validation when
useful. Biological interpretation and generalizability may remain uncertain.

Register comparisons, anticipated directions, and initial assessments before requesting analyses.
The controller assigns claim references. For a changed claim, propose a new comparison and link
refinements to the earlier parent claim.
Clinical log_pfs_months is natural log progression-free survival in months, fully observed without
censoring. Dependency scores are continuous; more negative values mean stronger dependency.
Research signatures are constructed standardized assays in arbitrary units. Research markers D, E,
and F are constructed binary assays with no assigned gene, pathway, or clinical role.
A mean_difference is exposed minus comparator within eligibility and subgroup. An interaction
subtracts that comparison in the subgroup complement in the same eligible population.
Use your scientific judgment to assess the size, uncertainty, and importance of each effect
and decide which conclusions the evidence supports. Explain your reasoning in the narrative.
Returned estimates and intervals are ALREADY SIGNED to the indicated hypothesis direction. Do not
multiply them by direction again. For example, raw -0.4 with direction -1 is reported as +0.4.
Discovery analyses use 95% Welch intervals and need at least 20 observations in every
comparison cell.

Each iteration has explore, analyze, appraise, and synthesize stages. Every stage may register
hypotheses for later analysis. Analyze selects up to 12 previously registered hypotheses.
Appraise assesses every new discovery result, records active/deferred/closed investigation, and may
request validation after considering those results. At most one new voluntary validation request
is allowed per iteration and ten per run. Cached requests reuse the same evidence. The evaluator
may also deliver scheduled validation during the run. Independent intervals account for the maximum
number of validation comparisons in the run. Results arrive before synthesis. Assess newly released
validation immediately in synthesis and explicitly reassess the original claim when its response
deadline appears in the context, even if you also investigate a refinement. The controller maintains
the accepted claim set from your assessments; you do not need to repeat that list. Explanations are
retained for inspection. Acceptance does not require prior independent validation.


You are investigating the supplied research dataset. Return one JSON object using
only this stage's response form. The service performs analyses; you choose the science.
For this task, a relative difference in outcome of 10% or greater is considered clinically significant.
Use your judgment about uncertainty and conclusions in light of this clinical significance threshold. Acceptance does not require
independent validation first. Explain your reasoning in narrative.

The ledger contains every registered claim, its current assessment, and all its available direct
evidence. References H1, H2, ... identify claims; R1, R2, ... identify evidence. Copy these short
references when needed. New proposals receive references automatically after this stage. A changed
comparison or reversed claim is a new proposal, optionally linked to an existing parent.
Proposal direction is the claim (+1 positive, -1 negative); anticipated_direction is your
expectation
of the raw exposed-minus-comparator contrast before seeing evidence (-1, 0 uncertain, +1).
initial_status is your assessment at registration. These initial judgments are recorded once.
If a proposal repeats an existing claim, the controller preserves that claim's current assessment;
use assessments to change a scientific conclusion.

For each claim in assessments_due, return one assessment with claim,
status (accept/reject/unresolved),
and investigation (active/deferred/closed). You may also reassess other claims. Omitted claims keep
their current assessment. Assess the original claim even when proposing a refinement or reversal.
By omitting evidence in an assessment, you assess all evidence displayed on that claim's card;
the controller attaches those references. To specify a subset or related evidence, provide evidence
with short R references; include the evidence listed in assessments_due for that claim.
An unchanged assessment or an investigation-only change can use evidence: [];
changing accept/reject/unresolved requires available evidence. Bookkeeping does not satisfy a due
evidence assessment.
For a refinement, parent identifies the earlier claim; omitted motivating_evidence attaches the
parent's displayed evidence. These automatic links record evidence supplied for your assessment
or refinement, not proof that you discussed or understood every result.

The controller maintains the accepted set from your assessments. Do not reconstruct it. Optional
research_notes replaces your persistent notebook; omit it to keep the existing notes. Use it for
plans or reasoning worth retaining. Latest stage narratives are also retained. All earlier numerical
evidence remains in the ledger. Do not repeat completed actions or old responses.
Omit unused fields.

Your action now: Propose scientifically useful new comparisons or refinements for later analysis.

  "narrative": "With the three large SMARCA2, WRN, and NFE2L2 associations now characterized and closed for practical purposes, the next step is to expand coverage toward biologically plausible predictor-outcome pairs and specificity controls. The strongest new candidates are mechanistically motivated synthetic-lethality or pathway dependencies. For dependency_TMED10, ER-Golgi trafficking can support receptor tyrosine kinase and secretory signaling; ERBB2-amplified lines may therefore show stronger TMED10 dependency, so I registered a negative direction. For dependency_WRN, I registered BRCA2 loss as an independent probe of DNA repair/replication stress synthetic lethality, restricted to MSI-negative lines to test whether a WRN association can exist apart from the accepted MSI-high effect. For dependency_NFE2L2, I registered the accepted KEAP1-loss effect within STK11-loss lines, a clinically relevant co-mutation context in lung adenocarcinoma, using the same weaker-dependency direction as the accepted KEAP1 association. MYC amplification is a broad proliferative and transcriptional driver, so I registered MYC amplification against dependency_STAT3 and dependency_KIF18A to test whether amplified MYC contexts depend more on STAT3 transcriptional programs or mitotic machinery. Cross-RTK relationships are also worth probing: EGFR-amplified lines may depend more on ERBB2 through receptor network coactivation, so I registered ERBB2 dependency against EGFR amplification. Finally, I added direct marker-null controls for WRN and NFE2L2 using markers D, E, and F. Use the supplied dataset to discover and follow up comparisons, assess effect sizes and uncertainty, and decide which conclusions the evidence supports. Use independent validation when useful and distinguish findings in this dataset from claims about causality or generalizability.
Each iteration proceeds through explore (propose comparisons), analyze (request tests), appraise (assess the resulting discovery evidence and optionally request validation), and synthesize (assess validation and update conclusions and plans).

Study instructions:
Investigate diverse, scientifically meaningful comparisons and use previous
results to allocate further investigation. Broad exploration and focused follow-up are both useful
throughout the run. Assess discoveries in this supplied dataset and use independent validation when
useful. Biological interpretation and generalizability may remain uncertain.

Register comparisons, anticipated directions, and initial assessments before requesting analyses.
The controller assigns claim references. For a changed claim, propose a new comparison and link
refinements to the earlier parent claim.
Clinical log_pfs_months is natural log progression-free survival in months, fully observed without
censoring. Dependency scores are continuous; more negative values mean stronger dependency.
Research signatures are constructed standardized assays in arbitrary units. Research markers D, E,
and F are constructed binary assays with no assigned gene, pathway, or clinical role.
A mean_difference is exposed minus comparator within eligibility and subgroup. An interaction
subtracts that comparison in the subgroup complement in the same eligible population.
Use your scientific judgment to assess the size, uncertainty, and importance of each effect
and decide which conclusions the evidence supports. Explain your reasoning in the narrative.
Returned estimates and intervals are ALREADY SIGNED to the indicated hypothesis direction. Do not
multiply them by direction again. For example, raw -0.4 with direction -1 is reported as +0.4.
Discovery analyses use 95% Welch intervals and need at least 20 observations in every
comparison cell.

Each iteration has explore, analyze, appraise, and synthesize stages. Every stage may register
hypotheses for later analysis. Analyze selects up to 12 previously registered hypotheses.
Appraise assesses every new discovery result, records active/deferred/closed investigation, and may
request validation after considering those results. At most one new voluntary validation request
is allowed per iteration and ten per run. Cached requests reuse the same evidence. The evaluator
may also deliver scheduled validation during the run. Independent intervals account for the maximum
number of validation comparisons in the run. Results arrive before synthesis. Assess newly released
validation immediately in synthesis and explicitly reassess the original claim when its response
deadline appears in the context, even if you also investigate a refinement. The controller maintains
the accepted claim set from your assessments; you do not need to repeat that list. Explanations are
retained for inspection. Acceptance does not require prior independent validation.


You are investigating the supplied research dataset. Return one JSON object using
only this stage's response form. The service performs analyses; you choose the science.
For this task, a relative difference in outcome of 10% or greater is considered clinically significant.
Use your judgment about uncertainty and conclusions in light of this clinical significance threshold. Acceptance does not require
independent validation first. Explain your reasoning in narrative.

The ledger contains every registered claim, its current assessment, and all its available direct
evidence. References H1, H2, ... identify claims; R1, R2, ... identify evidence. Copy these short
references when needed. New proposals receive references automatically after this stage. A changed
comparison or reversed claim is a new proposal, optionally linked to an existing parent.
Proposal direction is the claim (+1 positive, -1 negative); anticipated_direction is your
expectation
of the raw exposed-minus-comparator contrast before seeing evidence (-1, 0 uncertain, +1).
initial_status is your assessment at registration. These initial judgments are recorded once.
If a proposal repeats an existing claim, the controller preserves that claim's current assessment;
use assessments to change a scientific conclusion.

For each claim in assessments_due, return one assessment with claim,
status (accept/reject/unresolved),
and investigation (active/deferred/closed). You may also reassess other claims. Omitted claims keep
their current assessment. Assess the original claim even when proposing a refinement or reversal.
By omitting evidence in an assessment, you assess all evidence displayed on that claim's card;
the controller attaches those references. To specify a subset or related evidence, provide evidence
with short R references; include the evidence listed in assessments_due for that claim.
An unchanged assessment or an investigation-only change can use evidence: [];
changing accept/reject/unresolved requires available evidence. Bookkeeping does not satisfy a due
evidence assessment.
For a refinement, parent identifies the earlier claim; omitted motivating_evidence attaches the
parent's displayed evidence. These automatic links record evidence supplied for your assessment
or refinement, not proof that you discussed or understood every result.

The controller maintains the accepted set from your assessments. Do not reconstruct it. Optional
research_notes replaces your persistent notebook; omit it to keep the existing notes. Use it for
plans or reasoning worth retaining. Latest stage narratives are also retained. All earlier numerical
evidence remains in the ledger. Do not repeat completed actions or old responses.
Omit unused fields.

Your action now: Select up to 12 existing claim references in run_analyses. This requests analyses now; previously tested comparisons reuse their data and give no new sample. New results enter the ledger after this form is accepted and are assessed in appraise. Any assessment in this form must use evidence already in the supplied ledger.

For dependency_TMED10, ER-Golgi trafficking can support receptor tyrosine kinase and secretory signaling; ERBB2-amplified lines may therefore show stronger TMED10 dependency, so I registered a negative direction. For dependency_NFE2L2, I registered the accepted KEAP1-loss effect within STK11-loss lines, a clinically relevant co-mutation context in lung adenocarcinoma, using the same weaker-dependency direction as the accepted KEAP1 association. MYC amplification is a broad proliferative and transcriptional driver, so I registered MYC amplification against dependency_STAT3 and dependency_KIF18A to test whether amplified MYC contexts depend more on STAT3 transcriptional programs or mitotic machinery. Cross-RTK relationships are also worth probing: EGFR-amplified lines may depend more on ERBB2 through receptor network coactivation, so I registered ERBB2 dependency against EGFR amplification. Similarly, KRAS-mutant lines may bypass BRAF, giving a weaker BRAF dependency, and EGFR-amplified lines might exploit RIT1-related RAS/MAPK signaling; these are more exploratory but cell counts are adequate. CDKN2A loss is registered against MDM2 dependency because the CDKN2A locus includes p14ARF, an upstream regulator of the MDM2-p53 axis, though the direction is biologically complex and remains uncertain. Finally, I added direct marker-null controls for WRN and NFE2L2 using markers D, E, and F. These markers have no assigned biological role; near-zero associations would support that the large accepted effects are not driven by latent marker-defined structure, whereas substantial marker associations would caution against interpreting the accepted effects as specific to the intended biological predictors.
