record.narrative: The new discovery batch adds one very large new association, one clearly meaningful moderate association, and several mostly null or imprecise probes. H49, TP53 loss versus dependency_USP7, has signed estimate +0.802 (CI +0.782 to +0.822), which is far beyond any plausible 10% clinical threshold for USP7-scale outcomes and also far beyond null. I accept this as a strong same-dataset association and keep it active while requesting independent validation because it is a new large finding and independent confirmation would be scientifically valuable. H54, the accepted KEAP1-loss association restricted to STK11-loss lines, has signed estimate +0.775 (CI +0.727 to +0.823), supporting persistence of the large weaker-NFE2L2 effect in this co-mutation context; because the main KEAP1 effect is already accepted and heavily checked, this robustness claim is accepted and closed. H59, CDKN2A loss versus dependency_MDM2, has signed estimate +0.117 (CI +0.082 to +0.152); the lower bound exceeds the approximate 0.026 absolute 10% threshold for MDM2-scale outcomes, so I accept it as a meaningful dataset association and keep it active for future technical and specificity checks. H16 is clinically insignificant for the TP53-loss direction on RPL11: signed estimate +0.004 with upper bound +0.024 below the approximate 0.025 RPL11 threshold, so I reject it. H57, H58, and H37 are signed negative or near-null; their positive claim-direction upper bounds are well below outcome-scale 10% thresholds, so the hypothesized directions are rejected, even though the intervals may allow some opposite-direction signal. H14, H52, H53, and H56 are near-null but their intervals include values around or slightly above the relevant 10% thresholds, so I leave them unresolved but closed as low-yield follow-up checks. H51 is a marker-null direct control for marker F and dependency_NFE2L2; it is reassuringly near-null, but the interval still permits marginal positive and negative differences, so it remains unresolved and closed as specificity evidence. I did not request validation for the huge accepted H54, nor for the rejected or low-yield unresolved claims. I registered same-dataset technical robustness, marker-null, and one TP53 interaction proposal for the newly accepted H49 and H59 effects. All conclusions remain associations in the supplied lung-lineage dataset, not causal or generalizable claims.

Research goal: investigate which measured predictors and subgroups are associated with scientifically meaningful differences in dependency_BRAF (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_DHX9 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_EGFR (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_ERBB2 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_KIF18A (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_KRAS (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_MDM2 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_NFE2L2 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_POLR2A (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_RIT1 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_RPL11 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_SMARCA2 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_STAT3 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_TMED10 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_USP7 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_WRN (CRISPR dependency score). Use independent validation when useful and distinguish findings in this dataset from claims about causality or generalizability.
Each iteration proceeds through explore (propose comparisons), analyze (request tests), appraise (assess the resulting discovery evidence and optionally request validation), and synthesize (assess validation and update conclusions and plans).

Study instructions:
Investigate diverse, scientifically meaningful comparisons and use previous
results to allocate further investigation. Broad exploration and focused follow-up are both useful
throughout the run. Assess discoveries in this supplied dataset and use independent validation when
useful. Biological interpretation and generalizability may remain uncertain.

Register comparisons, anticipated directions, and initial assessments before requesting analyses.
The controller assigns claim references. For a changed claim, propose a new comparison and link
refinements to the earlier parent claim.
Clinical log_pfs_months is natural log progression-free survival in months, fully observed without
censoring. Dependency scores are continuous; more negative values mean stronger dependency.
Research signatures are constructed standardized assays in arbitrary units. Research markers D, E,
and F are constructed binary assays with no assigned gene, pathway, or clinical role.
A mean_difference is exposed minus comparator within eligibility and subgroup. An interaction
subtracts that comparison in the subgroup complement in the same eligible population.
Use your scientific judgment to assess the size, uncertainty, and importance of each effect
and decide which conclusions the evidence supports. Explain your reasoning in the narrative.
Returned estimates and intervals are ALREADY SIGNED to the indicated hypothesis direction. Do not
multiply them by direction again. For example, raw -0.4 with direction -1 is reported as +0.4.
Discovery analyses use 95% Welch intervals and need at least 20 observations in every
comparison cell.

Each iteration has explore, analyze, appraise, and synthesize stages. Every stage may register
hypotheses for later analysis. Analyze selects up to 12 previously registered hypotheses.
Appraise assesses every new discovery result, records active/deferred/closed investigation, and may
request validation after considering those results. At most one new voluntary validation request
is allowed per iteration and ten per run. Cached requests reuse the same evidence. The evaluator
may also deliver scheduled validation during the run. Independent intervals account for the maximum
number of validation comparisons in the run. Results arrive before synthesis. Assess newly released
validation immediately in synthesis and explicitly reassess the original claim when its response
deadline appears in the context, even if you also investigate a refinement. The controller maintains
the accepted claim set from your assessments; you do not need to repeat that list. Explanations are
retained for inspection. Acceptance does not require prior independent validation.


You are investigating the supplied research dataset. Return one JSON object using
only this stage's response form. The service performs analyses; you choose the science.
For this task, a relative difference in outcome of 10% or greater is considered clinically significant.
Use your judgment about uncertainty and conclusions in light of this clinical significance threshold. Acceptance does not require
independent validation first. Explain your reasoning in narrative.

The ledger contains every registered claim, its current assessment, and all its available direct
evidence. References H1, H2, ... identify claims; R1, R2, ... identify evidence. Copy these short
references when needed. New proposals receive references automatically after this stage. A changed
comparison or reversed claim is a new proposal, optionally linked to an existing parent.
Proposal direction is the claim (+1 positive, -1 negative); anticipated_direction is your
expectation
of the raw exposed-minus-comparator contrast before seeing evidence (-1, 0 uncertain, +1).
initial_status is your assessment at registration. These initial judgments are recorded once.
If a proposal repeats an existing claim, the controller preserves that claim's current assessment;
use assessments to change a scientific conclusion.

For each claim in assessments_due, return one assessment with claim,
status (accept/reject/unresolved),
and investigation (active/deferred/closed). You may also reassess other claims. Omitted claims keep
their current assessment. Assess the original claim even when proposing a refinement or reversal.
By omitting evidence in an assessment, you assess all evidence displayed on that claim's card;
the controller attaches those references. To specify a subset or related evidence, provide evidence
with short R references; include the evidence listed in assessments_due for that claim.
An unchanged assessment or an investigation-only change can use evidence: [];
changing accept/reject/unresolved requires available evidence. Bookkeeping does not satisfy a due
evidence assessment.
For a refinement, parent identifies the earlier claim; omitted motivating_evidence attaches the
parent's displayed evidence. These automatic links record evidence supplied for your assessment
or refinement, not proof that you discussed or understood every result.

The controller maintains the accepted set from your assessments. Do not reconstruct it. Optional
research_notes replaces your persistent notebook; omit it to keep the existing notes. Use it for
plans or reasoning worth retaining. Latest stage narratives are also retained. All earlier numerical
evidence remains in the ledger. Do not repeat completed actions or old responses.
Omit unused fields.

Your action now: Assess new validation and any response deadlines listed below. Explain what you conclude and what to investigate next. Accepted claims update automatically.

record.narrative:
The independent validation for H49 confirms the newly discovered TP53-loss association with dependency_USP7 and does so at a very large effect size. The discovery signed estimate was +0.802 (95% CI +0.782 to +0.822), and the independent validation signed estimate was +0.800 (strict independent interval +0.769 to +0.831). Because the signed direction is positive and dependency scores are more negative when stronger, this means TP53 loss is associated with much weaker USP7 dependency. The validation interval is far above any plausible 10% clinical-threshold magnitude on the USP7 scale and far from null, so I accept H49 as a robust same-dataset association and close further investigation of the main effect. This gives a fourth major accepted main association alongside SMARCA4-loss -> stronger SMARCA2 dependency, MSI-high -> stronger WRN dependency, and KEAP1-loss -> weaker NFE2L2 dependency. The accepted CDKN2A-loss -> stronger MDM2 association (H59) remains active mainly for technical robustness and biological-context probes.

For H15, the response deadline on the ERBB2-amplification -> dependency_STAT3 claim is now met by independent validation. The discovery signed estimate was +0.0222 (CI -0.0147 to +0.0592), and the validation signed estimate was +0.0243 (independent interval -0.0291 to +0.0776). For dependency_STAT3, whose observed mean is about -0.282, a 10% relative difference corresponds roughly to an absolute signed effect around +0.028 in the proposed direction. Both point estimates are below that threshold, and the validation interval includes null as well as a small opposite-direction effect. Therefore the validation does not rescue the borderline discovery signal. I do not accept the claim of a clinically meaningful ERBB2-amplification association with stronger STAT3 dependency. I leave it unresolved because the upper validation interval still permits a clinically meaningful positive difference, but I keep it closed because it is low priority and the combined evidence suggests a small or uncertain effect rather than a clear large one.

The current supported dataset-level findings are: SMARCA4 loss is associated with stronger SMARCA2 dependency; MSI-high is associated with stronger WRN dependency; KEAP1 loss is associated with weaker NFE2L2 dependency, including in STK11-loss lines and under independent validation of the high-quality-screen subset; TP53 loss is associated with weaker USP7 dependency; and CDKN2A loss is associated with stronger MDM2 dependency, supported by a discovery lower bound clearly above the approximate MDM2 10% threshold. These are associations within the supplied lung-lineage CRISPR dataset, not causal claims and not claims of external generalizability. The next most informative analyses are context and specificity probes for the newly accepted H49 and H59 effects: non-Avana screen robustness, TP53-status stratification of the CDKN2A-MDM2 effect, and marker-null controls. If those remain reassuring, future work can return to the remaining active subtype, MAPK, and ARID1A/SMARCA2 probes.

plans or reasoning worth retaining. Latest stage narratives are also retained. All earlier numerical
evidence remains in the ledger. Do not repeat completed actions or old responses.

The strongest new candidates are mechanistically motivated synthetic-lethality or pathway dependencies. For dependency_TMED10, ER-Golgi trafficking can support receptor tyrosine kinase and secretory signaling; ERBB2-amplified lines may therefore show stronger TMED10 dependency, so I registered a negative direction. For dependency_WRN, I registered BRCA2 loss as an independent probe of DNA repair/replication stress synthetic lethality, restricted to MSI-negative lines to test whether a WRN association can exist apart from the accepted MSI-high effect. For dependency_NFE2L2, I registered the accepted KEAP1-loss effect within STK11-loss lines, a clinically relevant co-mutation context in lung adenocarcinoma, using the same weaker-dependency direction as the accepted KEAP1 association. MYC amplification is a broad proliferative and transcriptional driver, so I registered MYC amplification against dependency_STAT3 and dependency_KIF18A to test whether amplified MYC contexts depend more on STAT3 transcriptional programs or mitotic machinery. Cross-RTK relationships are also worth probing: EGFR-amplified lines may depend more on ERBB2 through receptor network coactivation, so I registered ERBB2 dependency against EGFR amplification. Similarly, KRAS-mutant lines may bypass BRAF, giving a weaker BRAF dependency, and EGFR-amplified lines might exploit RIT1-related RAS/MAPK signaling; these are more exploratory but cell counts are adequate. CDKN2A loss is registered against MDM2 dependency because the CDKN2A locus includes p14ARF, an upstream regulator of the MDM2-p53 axis, though the direction is biologically complex and remains uncertain. Finally, I added direct marker-null controls for WRN and NFE2L2 using markers D, E, and F. These markers have no assigned biological role; near-zero associations would support that the large accepted effects are not driven by latent marker-defined structure, whereas substantial marker associations would caution against interpreting the accepted effects as specific to the intended biological predictors. All proposals are associations within the supplied lung-lineage dataset, not causal claims or claims of external generalizability.","analyze":"No assessments are due in this stage. H49, TP53 loss versus dependency_USP7, has signed estimate +0.802 (CI +0.782 to +0.822), which is far beyond any plausible 10% clinical threshold for USP7-scale outcomes and also far beyond null. I accept this as a strong same-dataset association and keep it active while requesting independent validation because it is a new large finding and independent confirmation would be scientifically valuable. H54, the accepted KEAP1-loss association restricted to STK11-loss lines, has signed estimate +0.775 (CI +0.727 to +0.823), supporting persistence of the large weaker-NFE2L2 effect in this co-mutation context; because the main KEAP1 effect is already accepted and heavily checked, this robustness claim is accepted and closed. H59, CDKN2A loss versus dependency_MDM2, has signed estimate +0.117 (CI +0.082 to +0.152); the lower bound exceeds the approximate 0.026 absolute 10% threshold for MDM2-scale outcomes, so I accept it as a meaningful dataset association and keep it active for future technical and specificity checks. H16 is clinically insignificant for the TP53-loss direction on RPL11: signed estimate +0.004 with upper bound +0.024 below the approximate 0.025 RPL11 threshold, so I reject it. H57, H58, and H37 are signed negative or near-null; their positive claim-direction upper bounds are well below outcome-scale 10% thresholds, so the hypothesized directions are rejected, even though the intervals may allow some opposite-direction signal. H14, H52, H53, and H56 are near-null but their intervals include values around or slightly above the relevant 10% thresholds, so I leave them unresolved but closed as low-yield follow-up checks. H51 is a marker-null direct control for marker F and dependency_NFE2L2; it is reassuringly near-null, but the interval still permits marginal positive and negative differences, so it remains unresolved and closed as specificity evidence. I did not request validation for the huge accepted H54, nor for the rejected or low-yield unresolved claims. All conclusions remain associations in the supplied lung-lineage dataset, not causal or generalizable claims.","synthesize":"The independent validation for H49 confirms the newly discovered TP53-loss association with dependency_USP7 and does so at a very large effect size. The discovery signed estimate was +0.802 (95% CI +0.782 to +0.822), and the independent validation signed estimate was +0.800 (strict independent interval +0.769 to +0.831). Because the signed direction is positive and dependency scores are more negative when stronger, this means TP53 loss is associated with much weaker USP7 dependency. The validation interval is far above any plausible 10% clinical-threshold magnitude on the USP7 scale and far from null, so I accept H49 as a robust same-dataset association and close further investigation of the main effect. This gives a fourth major accepted main association alongside SMARCA4-loss -> stronger SMARCA2 dependency, MSI-high -> stronger WRN dependency, and KEAP1-loss -> weaker NFE2L2 dependency. The accepted CDKN2A-loss -> stronger MDM2 association (H59) remains active mainly for technical robustness and biological-context probes.\n\nFor H15, the response deadline on the ERBB2-amplification -> dependency_STAT3 claim is now met by independent validation. The discovery signed estimate was +0.0222 (CI -0.0147 to +0.0592), and the validation signed estimate was +0.0243 (independent interval -0.0291 to +0.0776). For dependency_STAT3, whose observed mean is about -0.282, a 10% relative difference corresponds roughly to an absolute signed effect around +0.028 in the proposed direction. Both point estimates are below that threshold, and the validation interval includes null as well as a small opposite-direction effect. record.narrative:
The dataset now supports five major same-dataset associations: SMARCA4 loss is associated with stronger dependency_SMARCA2, MSI-high with stronger dependency_WRN, KEAP1 loss with weaker dependency_NFE2L2, TP53 loss with weaker dependency_USP7 after independent validation, and CDKN2A loss with stronger dependency_MDM2. The main effect of each accepted association has already been checked extensively, so the next scientifically useful work is specificity testing, co-deletion/context testing, and broadening coverage to less tested predictor-outcome pairs.

For the newly accepted CDKN2A-loss association with stronger dependency_MDM2, MTAP loss is an important co-deletion probe because MTAP is frequently co-deleted with CDKN2A. A strong MTAP-loss association would suggest that the MDM2 signal may reflect broader 9p21 deletion or linked genomic structure, whereas a near-null MTAP result would increase confidence that the association is more specific to CDKN2A loss or its regulatory products. I also registered missing marker-null direct controls for the newly accepted MDM2 and USP7 effects, for SMARCA2, and as part of the marker-specificity program. Markers D, E, and F have no assigned biology; near-zero associations would argue against the large accepted effects being driven by latent marker-defined structure, whereas substantial marker associations would caution against over-specific biological interpretation.

For SWI/SNF biology, I registered a direct ARID1A-loss versus dependency_SMARCA2 contrast. The accepted SMARCA4-loss effect is very large, but a direct ARID1A-loss effect would test whether the dependency is a broader SWI/SNF complex feature or more specific to SMARCA4 loss. I also registered SMARCA4 loss versus dependency_POLR2A to test a transcriptional dependency hypothesis: chromatin-remodeler loss may alter RNA polymerase II dependency. RB1 loss versus dependency_DHX9 tests whether replication/transcription stress associated with RB1 loss increases dependence on an RNA helicase resolving R loops. NF1 loss versus dependency_BRAF tests RAS/MAPK bypass: if NF1 loss activates upstream signaling, BRAF could become less essential, though the direction remains biologically contestable. STK11 loss versus dependency_NFE2L2, restricted to KEAP1 wild-type lines, tests whether STK11 loss has an independent association with NRF2-pathway dependency rather than merely reflecting co-occurring KEAP1 loss. Finally, ERBB2 amplification versus dependency_EGFR and a high-Cas9 refinement of RB1 loss versus dependency_KIF18A broaden coverage of RTK coactivation and a borderline mitotic dependency signal. All of these remain associations within the supplied lung-lineage CRISPR dataset, not causal or generalizable claims.

record.narrative:
No assessments are due in this stage. I request 12 discovery analyses that balance mechanistic specificity, technical/contextual robustness, and broader predictor-outcome coverage.

For the newly accepted CDKN2A-loss association with stronger dependency_MDM2, I test: MTAP co-deletion (H78) to assess whether the MDM2 signal is attributable specifically to CDKN2A loss or to broader 9p21 deletion; CDKN2A-loss effects stratified by TP53 status (H75 and H76) to test independence from TP53 loss and interpret potential p14ARF-p53-MDM2 pathway structure; and non-Avana library robustness (H74) to address technical heterogeneity. Marker D direct control on dependency_MDM2 (H80) tests whether latent marker-defined structure can mimic the CDKN2A-MDM2 association.

For the accepted TP53-loss/USP7 association, I request marker D control (H77) as a negative-control specificity check for the newly validated USP7 signal.

For SWI/SNF biology, H83 directly tests ARID1A loss versus dependency_SMARCA2, whereas H85 tests whether SMARCA4 loss also affects dependency_POLR2A. These complement the accepted SMARCA4-SMARCA2 association by testing broader complex dependence and transcriptional dependency.

The remaining selected analyses broaden coverage with biologically motivated probes: RB1 loss versus dependency_DHX9 (H84) tests replication/transcription-stress dependence; NF1 loss versus dependency_BRAF (H86) tests RAS/MAPK bypass and weakened BRAF dependency; STK11 loss versus dependency_NFE2L2 within KEAP1 wild-type lines (H87) tests whether STK11 loss has an association apart from KEAP1; and RB1 loss versus dependency_KIF18A under high Cas9 activity (H88) refines a borderline mitotic signal. All selected claims are new evidence requests and are interpreted as associations within the supplied dataset, not causal or generalizable claims.

record.narrative:
The new batch primarily strengthens the accepted CDKN2A-loss association with stronger MDM2 dependency and gives one unexpected RB1-DHX9 signal in the opposite direction to the registered hypothesis.

For MDM2 specificity and robustness, H75 shows CDKN2A loss in TP53-loss-negative lines with signed estimate +0.119 (95% CI +0.079 to +0.158), and H76 shows CDKN2A loss in TP53-loss lines with signed estimate +0.111 (95% CI +0.035 to +0.186). Both lower bounds exceed the approximate absolute 10% MDM2 threshold (~0.027), so the association is accepted in both TP53 strata. H74 in non-Avana screens gives +0.125 (95% CI +0.029 to +0.222), also above threshold, although with small cells and wider uncertainty. Together with H59, these results make broader technical or TP53-status explanations less plausible, though the non-Avana estimate is imprecise and should not be overinterpreted.

MTAP co-deletion is not near enough to explain the CDKN2A effect to warrant further priority follow-up: H78 has signed estimate +0.019 (95% CI -0.008 to +0.045), far smaller than the CDKN2A effect but still permitting a clinically meaningful MTAP association. I mark it unresolved but closed. Marker controls are also reassuringly small: H80 for marker D on MDM2 gives +0.019 (95% CI -0.001 to +0.039), and H77 for marker D on USP7 gives +0.005 (95% CI -0.027 to +0.038). These do not support the large accepted effects being driven by marker-defined latent structure, but because the intervals still include threshold-scale effects, I keep them unresolved and closed as specificity evidence rather than accept a strict null.

For other probes, H83 ARID1A loss versus dependency_SMARCA2 fails the proposed stronger-dependency direction: signed estimate -0.017 with upper bound +0.023, below the SMARCA2 threshold (~0.042). I reject that original claim, while noting a possible opposite-direction signal. H85 SMARCA4 loss versus dependency_POLR2A also fails its proposed direction: upper bound +0.014 below the POLR2A threshold (~0.026), so I reject it as low-yield. H84 RB1 loss versus dependency_DHX9 was registered for stronger DHX9 dependency, but the signed interval is entirely negative (-0.061 to -0.009), with magnitude exceeding the DHX9 threshold (~0.025) in the opposite direction, suggesting RB1 loss is associated with weaker DHX9 dependency. I reject the original claim and register a reversal for later analysis.

H86 NF1 loss versus dependency_BRAF remains a biologically plausible borderline positive signal: +0.021 (95% CI -0.005 to +0.047), around the BRAF threshold (~0.025). I leave it active because validation or future context work may clarify it. H87 STK11 loss versus dependency_NFE2L2 in KEAP1-wild-type lines is near-null and does not support an independent STK11 effect in the proposed direction; because the interval still allows small threshold-scale effects, I mark it unresolved but closed. H88 high-Cas9 RB1 loss versus dependency_KIF18A is imprecise and opposite to the proposed direction; I close it as low-yield.

I request independent validation for H59, the main CDKN2A-loss versus dependency_MDM2 association, because it is a new accepted meaningful effect and independent confirmation is more valuable now than validating a borderline secondary context. All conclusions remain associations in this supplied lung-lineage dataset.

record.narrative:
The two due validation items strengthen the current core findings. For H24, KEAP1 loss in high-quality screens versus dependency_NFE2L2, the high-quality discovery signed estimate was +0.790 (95% CI +0.763 to +0.816), and the strict independent validation signed estimate was +0.799 (independent interval +0.759 to +0.839). Because the direction is positive on a negative-valued dependency score, this corresponds to much weaker NFE2L2 dependency in KEAP1-loss lines. The independent interval is extremely far from null and far above any plausible 10% clinical threshold on the NFE2L2 scale, so H24 remains accepted and is closed. This reinforces the broader accepted KEAP1-loss association while remaining limited to the supplied lung-lineage CRISPR dataset.

For H59, CDKN2A loss versus dependency_MDM2, the discovery signed estimate was +0.117 (95% CI +0.082 to +0.152), and the independent validation signed estimate was +0.116 (independent interval +0.065 to +0.166). For dependency_MDM2, whose absolute scale is roughly near -0.27, the approximate 10% clinical threshold is about 0.027 in signed magnitude. Both discovery and validation lower bounds exceed that threshold, and the intervals are consistent. Since this claim direction is negative on the raw score, the accepted interpretation is that CDKN2A-loss lines have more negative MDM2 dependency scores, i.e. stronger MDM2 dependency. I therefore accept H59, close the main effect, and retain it as one of the main same-dataset associations.

The supported dataset-level core associations are now: SMARCA4 loss is associated with stronger SMARCA2 dependency; MSI-high is associated with stronger WRN dependency; KEAP1 loss is associated with weaker NFE2L2 dependency, with robust support in high-quality and other technical contexts and independent validation of the high-quality subset; TP53 loss is associated with weaker USP7 dependency, independently validated; and CDKN2A loss is associated with stronger MDM2 dependency, independently validated. These are associations within this dataset, not causal claims and not claims of external generalizability.

The most informative next unresolved signal is H90, the reversal of H84. RB1 loss was not associated with stronger DHX9 dependency as originally hypothesized; instead, the reversal shows a positive signed raw difference of +0.0348 (95% CI +0.0091 to +0.0605), suggesting weaker DHX9 dependency in RB1-loss lines. The point estimate exceeds the approximate 0.025 DHX9 threshold, but the lower bound is below threshold and uncertainty is nontrivial, so I keep H90 active for same-dataset robustness and likely validation. H86, NF1 loss versus weaker BRAF dependency, remains borderline: +0.0211 with interval -0.0046 to +0.0468, around but not clearly above the approximate 0.025 BRAF threshold. It remains active but lower priority than H90.

Several probes produced negative or low-yield results. ARID1A loss did not support the hypothesized stronger SMARCA2 dependency, and SMARCA4 loss did not support a stronger POLR2A dependency in the registered direction. MTAP co-deletion was much smaller than the CDKN2A effect, and marker controls were near-null relative to the accepted large effects, though they do not strictly exclude small clinically meaningful marker associations. I defer most remaining active marker-null, technical robustness, subtype, and RTK probes because they are less informative than completing validation/robustness for the newly emerging RB1-DHX9 reversal and clarifying NF1-BRAF. The next analyses should focus on whether H90 and H86 survive screen-library, Cas9-activity, and screen-quality restrictions, with H90 as the primary validation candidate.

Study instructions:
Investigate diverse, scientifically meaningful comparisons and use previous
results to allocate further investigation. Broad exploration and focused follow-up are both useful

Register comparisons, anticipated directions, and initial assessments before requesting analyses.
The controller assigns claim references. For a changed claim, propose a new comparison and link
refinements to the earlier parent claim.
Clinical log_pfs_months is natural log progression-free survival in months, fully observed without
censoring. Dependency scores are continuous; more negative values mean stronger dependency.

and decide which conclusions the evidence supports. Explain your reasoning in the narrative.

comparison cell.

hypotheses for later analysis. Analyze selects up to 12 previously registered hypotheses.

request validation after considering those results. At most one new voluntary validation request
is allowed per iteration and ten per run. Cached requests reuse the same evidence. The evaluator
may also deliver scheduled validation during the run. Independent intervals account for the maximum
number of validation comparisons in the run. Results arrive before synthesis. Assess newly released
validation immediately in synthesis and explicitly reassess the original claim when its response
deadline appears in the context, even if you also investigate a refinement. The controller maintains
the accepted claim set from your assessments; you do not need to repeat that list. Explanations are
retained for inspection. Acceptance does not require prior independent validation.


You are investigating the supplied research dataset. Return one JSON object using
only this stage's response form. The service performs analyses; you choose the science.
For this task, a relative difference in outcome of 10% or greater is considered clinically significant.
Use your judgment about uncertainty and conclusions in light of this clinical significance threshold. Acceptance does not require
independent validation first. Explain your reasoning in narrative.

The ledger contains every registered claim, its current assessment, and all its available direct
evidence. References H1, H2, ... identify claims; R1, R2, ... identify evidence. Copy these short
references when needed. New proposals receive references automatically after this stage. A changed

expectation
of the raw exposed-minus-comparator contrast before seeing evidence (-1, 0 uncertain, +1).

If a proposal repeats an existing claim, the controller preserves that claim's current assessment;
use assessments to change a scientific conclusion.

For each claim in assessments_due, return one assessment with claim,
status (accept/reject/unresolved),
and investigation (active/deferred/closed). You may also reassess other claims. Omitted claims keep
their current assessment. Assess the original claim even when proposing a refinement or reversal.

For a refinement, parent identifies the earlier claim; omitted motivating_evidence attaches the
parent's displayed evidence. These automatic links record evidence supplied for your assessment
or refinement, not proof that you discussed or understood every result.

The controller maintains the accepted set from your assessments. Do not reconstruct it. Optional
research_notes replaces your persistent notebook; omit it to keep the existing notes. Use it for
plans or reasoning worth retaining. Latest stage narratives are also retained. All earlier numerical
evidence remains in the ledger. Do not repeat completed actions or old responses.
Omit unused fields.

Your action now: Propose scientifically useful new comparisons or refinements for later analysis.

record.narrative:
No assessments are due, and I request 12 previously registered untested discovery analyses. These analyses balance focused follow-up on the most informative unresolved signals with broader mechanistic coverage.

The primary priority is H90, the reversal of H84: RB1 loss was associated with weaker DHX9 dependency in the overall lung-lineage dataset (signed estimate +0.0348; 95% CI +0.0091 to +0.0605). Because the point estimate is above the approximate 10% clinical threshold on the DHX9 absolute-scale (~0.025) but the lower bound is below threshold, the signal is plausible but not yet robust enough to accept. The requested analyses test whether this signal persists in higher-quality or more homogeneous technical contexts and whether it is specific to RB1 loss rather than a byproduct of TP53 co-alteration or latent marker-defined structure. H91 tests Avana-library screens; H92 tests high-Cas9 screens; H93 tests high screen-quality screens. H96 and H97 stratify by TP53 loss to test whether the RB1-DHX9 association occurs independently of TP53 status. H98 is a marker-D null control for dependency_DHX9: because marker D has no assigned biology, a large marker-D association would caution that the apparent RB1-DHX9 signal may reflect non-specific latent assay structure, whereas a near-null marker-D contrast would increase confidence that the RB1 association is not a generic marker artifact.

The secondary priority is H86, NF1 loss versus weaker BRAF dependency. The overall estimate is borderline (signed estimate +0.0211; 95% CI -0.0046 to +0.0468), near the approximate BRAF threshold (~0.025) but not clearly above threshold. H94 tests Avana-library screens, H95 tests high-Cas9 screens, and H99 provides a marker-D null control for dependency_BRAF. If the NF1-BRAF association weakens in stringent subsets or marker-D shows a similarly large effect, the claim should be de-prioritized. If it persists and marker-D remains near-null, it may merit later validation.

I also use the remaining slots for biologically motivated broad exploration. H100 tests whether NF1 loss is associated with weaker KRAS dependency, reflecting possible MAPK-pathway bypass or reduced reliance on upstream KRAS signaling. H101 tests whether BRAF V600E is associated with weaker KRAS dependency, a related downstream MAPK bypass hypothesis. H102 tests STK11 loss versus stronger STAT3 dependency, motivated by LKB1/mTOR/AMPK-related stress signaling and possible STAT3 involvement. All requested estimates will come from Welch independent-cell comparisons with 95% intervals and cell-size diagnostics; conclusions remain limited to associations within the supplied lung-lineage CRISPR dataset, not causality or external generalizability.

I defer H103, PTEN loss versus dependency_STAT3, because it is similar in pathway focus to H102 but less immediately complementary to the active MAPK and specificity work. The H90 validation decision will primarily depend on whether H91, H92, H93, H96, and H97 maintain positive estimates with bounds near or above threshold, and whether H98 is near-null.

independent validation first. Explain your reasoning in narrative.

record.narrative: I audited the new evidence as critical reviewer. The RB1-loss and dependency_DHX9 signal remains the most informative unresolved claim, but these new analyses are mostly subset or marker-control tests and do not by themselves establish a clinically robust effect. H91 in Avana-library screens gives +0.0389 (95% CI +0.0126 to +0.0653), and H92 in high-Cas9 screens gives +0.0524 (+0.0159 to +0.0890). Because these are direction +1, positive values indicate weaker DHX9 dependency in RB1-loss lines. The intervals exclude null and are supportive, but their lower bounds remain below the approximate 10% DHX9 scale (~0.025), so I keep them unresolved. H93 in high screen-quality screens gives +0.0192 (-0.0121 to +0.0506), which is below threshold and imprecise; this does not reject the effect but weakens the claim of general robustness, so I defer it rather than prioritize further same-dataset subset work. record.narrative:
The newly delivered validation responses materially change the current conclusions. First, H49 was already an accepted discovery association: TP53-loss lines had higher, less-negative dependency_USP7 scores than TP53-loss-negative lines, interpreted as weaker USP7 dependency. The independent validation estimate is very consistent with discovery: signed validation estimate +0.800 with independent interval +0.769 to +0.831, compared with discovery +0.802, +0.782 to +0.822. This effect is extremely large relative to any approximate 10% clinical-scale threshold for dependency_USP7 and the validation interval remains far from both null and threshold-scale null. I therefore accept H49 and close it as a supported same-dataset association, with no causal or external generalizability claim.

Second, H36, MYC amplification versus dependency_RPL11, was already rejected on discovery evidence because the registered stronger-dependency direction was not supported by the discovery interval. The independent validation does not rescue the claim: the signed validation estimate is small, +0.015, with independent interval -0.015 to +0.044. For the registered direction, this is not a clinically meaningful robust effect, and the validation is inconsistent with the discovery direction. I keep H36 rejected and closed as a negative/low-yield probe.

Third, H90, the reversal of H84 for RB1 loss versus dependency_DHX9, was the key unresolved signal. H90 claimed that RB1-loss lines have weaker DHX9 dependency, i.e. higher and less-negative dependency_DHX9 scores. Discovery gave a suggestive positive signed estimate +0.0348, interval +0.0091 to +0.0605. The point estimate exceeded the approximate 10% DHX9 threshold (~0.025), but the lower bound was below threshold, motivating independent validation. The independent validation estimate is -0.0069, independent interval -0.0446 to +0.0309. Thus the validation point estimate is near zero and opposite to the claim, and the interval includes null, clinically meaningful positive effects, and clinically meaningful negative effects. Taken as a whole, the overall RB1-loss/DHX9 association is not supported as scientifically meaningful: discovery was borderline, the strict subset evidence was heterogeneous, and independent validation failed. I therefore reject H90 and close the investigation. The related same-dataset subset claims H91, H92, H93, H96, and H97 remain unresolved as exploratory subset estimates but are closed from active follow-up because they no longer provide a robust route to an accepted overall association.

The supported core same-dataset associations remain: SMARCA4 loss is associated with stronger SMARCA2 dependency; MSI-high is associated with stronger WRN dependency; KEAP1 loss is associated with weaker NFE2L2 dependency, with independent validation in the high-screen-quality subset; TP53 loss is associated with weaker USP7 dependency, now independently validated; and CDKN2A loss is associated with stronger MDM2 dependency, independently validated. Negative or low-yield results include the overall RB1-DHX9 reversal, MYC-amplification versus dependency_RPL11, ARID1A-loss versus dependency_SMARCA2 in the registered direction, SMARCA4-loss versus dependency_POLR2A in the registered direction, and marker-D positive associations used as specificity controls. The NF1-loss versus BRAF claim is closed as unresolved low-yield after borderline discovery and non-supportive robustness checks.

The most informative next analysis is the already registered but untested PTEN-loss versus dependency_STAT3 comparison. STAT3 has had only weak or borderline probes so far, and PTEN loss provides a mechanistically distinct PI3K/AKT/mTOR-related perturbation that could test whether STAT3 dependency is context-dependent in this dataset. If PTEN loss yields a discovery effect clearly above the approximate STAT3 clinical scale and with interval bounds supportive of clinical significance, I would consider accepting it without validation or requesting validation if the interval remains near threshold. If it is null or inconsistent, I would close the STAT3 pathway family and return to broader coverage of less-tested predictors and outcomes. All conclusions remain limited to associations in this supplied lung-lineage CRISPR dataset, not causal mechanisms or generalizable biology.

The registered but untested PTEN-loss versus dependency_STAT3 claim remains active and should be considered alongside this new set. To broaden mechanistically motivated coverage, I registered a set of falsifiable MAPK/PI3K, DNA-repair/replication-stress, LKB1-cell-cycle, and RAS-GTPase probes. For dependency scores, more negative values mean stronger dependency; therefore, for registered weaker-dependency claims I used direction +1 because the raw exposed-minus-comparator contrast would be positive, while for stronger-dependency claims I used direction -1 because the raw contrast would be negative. The approximate 10% clinical-scale thresholds, based on absolute outcome means, are roughly 0.025 for EGFR, KRAS, DHX9, POLR2A, KIF18A, RIT1, and RPL11; about 0.028 for STAT3; and about 0.030 for WRN. Because controller outputs are already signed to the registered direction, evidence supporting a claim should be positive and ideally have interval support above these approximate thresholds. The central lung-signaling hypotheses are that KRAS mutation or PI3K-pathway activation can bypass upstream EGFR dependence, whereas RTK amplification may increase dependence on downstream KRAS. ERBB2 amplification versus KRAS dependence is deliberately left with uncertain anticipated direction because HER2 signaling could either engage KRAS-associated MAPK signaling or bypass it through PI3K/AKT-related programs. The BRCA2-loss probes test DNA-repair synthetic-lethality-like associations with DHX9 and POLR2A; I restricted the WRN and BRCA2-DHX9/POLR2A probes to MSI-non-high lines to reduce confounding by the very strong MSI-high-WRN association and by MSI co-occurrence. The NF1-loss and MYC-amplification probes test whether increased RAS pathway activity or replication-stress states increase STAT3 or WRN dependence. The BRAF V600E versus RIT1 claim is a reversal of the earlier untested registered hypothesis: downstream BRAF activation may reduce dependence on the more upstream RIT1 GTPase, although pathway addiction to upstream RAS signaling remains an alternative. All comparisons are associations within this supplied lung-lineage CRISPR dataset only; they are not causal claims and do not imply external generalizability.

For dependency scores, more negative values mean stronger dependency; therefore, for registered weaker-dependency claims I used direction +1 because the raw exposed-minus-comparator contrast would be positive, while for stronger-dependency claims I used direction -1 because the raw contrast would be negative. H91 in Avana-library screens gives +0.0389 (95% CI +0.0126 to +0.0653), and H92 in high-Cas9 screens gives +0.0524 (+0.0159 to +0.0890). Because these are direction +1, positive values indicate weaker DHX9 dependency in RB1-loss lines. The intervals exclude null and are supportive, but their lower bounds remain below the approximate 10% DHX9 scale (~0.025), so I keep them unresolved. H93 in high screen-quality screens gives +0.0192 (-0.0121 to +0.0506), which is below threshold and imprecise; this does not reject the effect but weakens the claim of general robustness, so I defer it rather than prioritize further same-dataset subset work. TP53 stratification is informative: H96 gives +0.0513 (+0.0022 to +0.1004) in TP53-loss lines and H97 gives +0.0288 (-0.0013 to +0.0589) in TP53-loss-negative lines. Both are positive, arguing against a purely TP53-co-loss explanation, but both are wide and not convincingly above the clinical threshold. H98 marker-D control for DHX9 gives -0.0102 (-0.0261 to +0.0057), far below a clinically meaningful positive marker-D effect, so I reject the registered positive marker-D DHX9 association and close it as a specificity check. The RB1-DHX9 reversal was not supported by independent validation, so I am not proposing further RB1-DHX9 work unless a new independent reason appears. The registered but untested PTEN-loss versus dependency_STAT3 claim remains active and should be considered alongside this new set. To broaden mechanistically motivated coverage, I registered a set of falsifiable MAPK/PI3K, DNA-repair/replication-stress, LKB1-cell-cycle, and RAS-GTPase probes. For dependency scores, more negative values mean stronger dependency; therefore, for registered weaker-dependency claims I used direction +1 because the raw exposed-minus-comparator contrast would be positive, while for stronger-dependency claims I used direction -1 because the raw contrast would be negative. The approximate 10% clinical-scale thresholds, based on absolute outcome means, are roughly 0.025 for EGFR, KRAS, DHX9, POLR2A, KIF18A, RIT1, and RPL11; about 0.028 for STAT3; and about 0.030 for WRN. Because controller outputs are already signed to the registered direction, evidence supporting a claim should be positive and ideally have interval support above these approximate thresholds. The central lung-signaling hypotheses are that KRAS mutation or PI3K-pathway activation can bypass upstream EGFR dependence, whereas RTK amplification may increase dependence on downstream KRAS. ERBB2 amplification versus KRAS dependence is deliberately left with uncertain anticipated direction because HER2 signaling could either engage KRAS-associated MAPK signaling or bypass it through PI3K/AKT-related programs. The BRCA2-loss probes test DNA-repair synthetic-lethality-like associations with DHX9 and POLR2A; I restricted the WRN and BRCA2-DHX9/POLR2A probes to MSI-non-high lines to reduce confounding by the very strong MSI-high-WRN association and by MSI co-occurrence. To broaden mechanistically motivated coverage, I registered a set of falsifiable MAPK/PI3K, DNA-repair/replication-stress, LKB1-cell-cycle, and RAS-GTPase probes. For dependency scores, more negative values mean stronger dependency; therefore, for registered weaker-dependency claims I used direction +1 because the raw exposed-minus-comparator contrast would be positive, while for stronger-dependency claims I used direction -1 because the raw contrast would be negative. The approximate 10% clinical-scale thresholds, based on absolute outcome means, are roughly 0.025 for EGFR, KRAS, DHX9, POLR2A, KIF18A, RIT1, and RPL11; about 0.028 for STAT3; and about 0.030 for WRN. Because controller outputs are already signed to the registered direction, evidence supporting a claim should be positive and ideally have interval support above these approximate thresholds. record.narrative:
The new validation results resolve the due responses and materially strengthen two accepted same-dataset associations. For H59, CDKN2A loss versus dependency_MDM2, the independent validation evidence R65 gives a signed estimate of +0.1155 with an independent interval of +0.0653 to +0.1658. Because H59 is registered in the stronger-dependency direction (-1), this means CDKN2A-loss lines have more negative dependency_MDM2 scores than CDKN2A-intact lines, i.e. stronger MDM2 dependency. The magnitude is far above the approximate 10% scale threshold for dependency_MDM2 (~0.027), and the independent lower bound remains well above threshold. This is highly consistent with discovery R48 (+0.1169, +0.0823 to +0.1516). I therefore accept H59 and close it as a supported association within the supplied lung-lineage CRISPR dataset, not as a causal or externally generalizable claim.

For H103, PTEN loss versus dependency_STAT3, the newly delivered validation evidence R92 gives a signed estimate of +0.2831 with an independent interval of +0.2083 to +0.3580. H103 is also registered in the stronger-dependency direction (-1), so this indicates that PTEN-loss lines have substantially stronger STAT3 dependency than PTEN-intact lines. The discovery estimate R80 was +0.2674 (+0.2153 to +0.3195). The validation point estimate and interval are concordant, very precise relative to the approximate STAT3 10% threshold (~0.028), and the independent lower bound is far above both null and threshold. I therefore accept H103 with high confidence as a same-dataset association and close it.

The supported core associations now include SMARCA4 loss with stronger SMARCA2 dependency, MSI-high with stronger WRN dependency, KEAP1 loss with weaker NFE2L2 dependency, TP53 loss with weaker USP7 dependency, CDKN2A loss with stronger MDM2 dependency, and PTEN loss with stronger STAT3 dependency. The last two are now independently validated, along with TP53-UPP7 and KEAP1-NFE2L2 evidence from prior scheduled/validation comparisons.

Unresolved uncertainty remains mainly around borderline secondary signals. H116, the reversal of H111 for MYC amplification versus dependency_WRN among MSI-non-high lines, remains active but unresolved: the signed estimate is +0.0277, interval +0.0051 to +0.0503, relative to the approximate WRN 10% threshold (~0.030). This suggests weaker WRN dependency in MYC-amplified MSI-non-high lines, but the point estimate is just below threshold and the lower bound is also below threshold, so I do not accept it without further clarification. H113, ERBB2 amplification versus dependency_KRAS in the registered weaker-dependency direction, remains active and untested. Low-yield MAPK/PI3K bypass probes, RB1-DHX9, MYC-RPL11, and several DNA-repair/LKB1/STAT3 probes remain negative or closed as not providing robust same-dataset associations. All conclusions remain associations within this supplied lung-lineage dataset; they are not causal claims and do not imply generalizability.

For the next investigation, I registered a focused conditional probe of the newly accepted PTEN-STAT3 signal: PTEN loss versus stronger STAT3 dependency among PIK3CA-mutation-negative lines. This tests whether the PTEN effect is robust across PI3K-pathway context rather than being confined to PIK3CA-mutant co-alterations. I also leave H116 active because it is the most informative borderline unresolved signal if independent validation can be requested, and H113 active as a mechanistically motivated untested RTK-downstream probe.
